gaps.description: Inject known-good, known-neutral and known-harmful edits (synthetic ground truth, as CAR does for attribution; plus real edits with hidden held-out outcomes) into existing loops and report per gate: false-commit rate, harmful-commit rate, missed-improvement rate, evals-per-decision, safety-decay, and retention/forgetting under matched budget, with a task-level-search baseline. Cheap, paper-worthy, and it makes every other gap measurable. Reef just opened the need (#357/#358, 2026-09-09) and PACE defined the first two metrics.
gaps.evidence: No existing benchmark measures the acceptor: HarnessDev (2609.01437) scores harness creation/evolution; EvoHarnessBench (2609.04280) finds harness-induced forgetting; Aspire/S3Gym score self-evolution from vague goals; AI4AI-Bench and RSI-Exam score research-loop outcomes; AI2 'Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution' shows methods must be compared to task-level search under matched budgets; 'Simple Baselines are Competitive' shows search-space design dominates; EvoTrace finds ~30% of added lines are re-introductions of deleted code and BO on one program matches whole runs. Meanwhile headline gains sit inside noise (Meta-Harness +1.7pt within noise; HGM 56.7 vs 53.3 = 2 tasks on 60, single run; Hyperagents DGM-H vs DGM-custom n.s. with 5 seeds; Self-Harness 132% vs a 3-sentence baseline; SkillOpt-Sleep 18-cell mean within noise). PACE's greedy 30-42% false-commit number is the only acceptor-level measurement in the field and it is on toy models.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Papers are rewarded for the agent's score, not the gate's; injecting known-bad edits requires owning the loop's accept() call-site, which most systems do not expose; synthetic-ground-truth design is fiddly; Reef's benchmark tasks were only filed two days ago.
gaps.who_cares: Reef, agentdescent, auto-harness, Self-Harness, GEPA maintainers choosing a gate; reviewers at the ICLR RSI workshop and the AI2/UW evaluation-methodology group; anyone deciding whether to turn on an unattended learning loop.

gaps.title: Post-acceptance monitoring with automatic revert (shadow/canary deployment of self-modifications)
gaps.description: Accept() is only half the gate: serve the candidate artifact to a fraction of sessions (or shadow-evaluate it on incoming tasks), compare against the incumbent with the same paired statistics, auto-revert on regression, and tag known-safe checkpoints for multi-step rollback. Most systems already have snapshots or ledgers; what is missing is the trigger that fires them and depth >1. Cheap where a ledger exists (Hermes, Prime, SkillClaw, EvoMap, Reef).
gaps.evidence: Reef: rollback is one step deep, rechecks periodic/manual, weight path AlwaysSelect. AHE: attribution verdicts HARMFUL/INEFFECTIVE shown to the LLM but no code reverts; regression prediction near random. SkillOpt-Sleep#247: no revert after adopt. Gödel Agent: modified solver goes live regardless of validation score. Continual Harness: every Refiner edit incl. wholesale prompt rewrites accepted unconditionally, Red regressed. ACE: every curator ADD applied; helpful/harmful counters never used to remove content. R-Zero/Dr. Zero: main.sh blindly chains iterations though performance peaks at iter 2-3 (3B EM 32.0->28.4). Hermes has per-mutation ledger rollback that fails closed but nothing triggers it. Misevolve Appendix B proposes tagged known-safe checkpoints, never implemented. Adaptive Auto-Harness documents that naive continuous updates 'peak early and then decline'.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Requires the same outcome signal the gate lacks, so it inherits Gaps 2 and 6; canary serving needs session routing that single-user CLIs do not have; and researchers stop the run when the curve looks good, so the decline phase is rarely instrumented.
gaps.who_cares: Production accumulators (Hermes, Prime, OpenViking, SkillClaw) whose users cannot tell which of last week's skills broke this week; Reef and agentdescent as release-pipeline infra; weight-level loops (R-Zero, Dr. Zero, AgentEvolver) with documented iteration-k+1 declines.

gaps.title: When NOT to evolve: cost/benefit-gated triggers and utility-tied retirement instead of schedule- or prompt-driven writing
gaps.description: Replace 'be ACTIVE' prompts and fixed schedules with a trigger that fires on measured stagnation or repeated failure signatures, a prior on expected lift minus eval cost, cross-session dedupe, and retirement of artifacts whose attributed utility stays ~0. Cheap once the loop-health funnel exists; it directly reduces the churn that PACE identifies as the symptom of uncontrolled acceptance.
gaps.evidence: Hermes: review prompt biased toward acting ('be ACTIVE'), users report over-writing and nudge floods (#70128, #99661), ~30K tokens per fork at zero yield during #95976. Continual Harness: Refiner is schedule-driven (every 25/100 steps) not stagnation-triggered; create-forget-focus-fix funnel. Adaptive Auto-Harness (2606.01770): naive continuous harness updates make accuracy peak early then decline; decomposes evolution loss vs adaptation loss. EvoHarnessBench: harness-induced forgetting when capabilities are added. AutoResearchClaw ablation: cross-run memory buys -0.48 quality vs robust inner loops -1.37/-40% completion — invest in in-run repair before cross-run evolution. ACE: playbooks bloat past 100K tokens with DELETE/MERGE as TODO stubs. Voyager/ReasoningBank: append-only with no pruning. The self-evolving-agents survey (2507.21046) names 'no treatment of when not to evolve' as an open gap.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Product incentive is visible activity ('your agent learned 12 things today'); without attribution there is no utility to tie retirement to; and cost is borne by the user's API bill, not the framework author.
gaps.who_cares: Hermes/ECC/OpenViking users paying for zero-yield learning; enterprise buyers of 'self-evolving' features who need bounded drift; benchmark authors measuring retention (EvoHarnessBench, Evo-Memory).

surprising_observations: Hermes' flagship learning loop was not broken by a missing fitness function but by two SAFETY guards interacting (read-before-write × skill_view repeat-view dedup, hermes-agent#95976): 100% of skill updates refused, for weeks, with the per-fork result logged and nobody alerted. Safety machinery and loop-health telemetry are coupled — every guard you add needs a probe that the guard did not kill learning.

Camp B's evaluation-integrity failures are all the same bug and it is not an AI problem: the proposer's filesystem view includes the evaluator or its data (DGM#35 hidden tests in /polyglot, Hyperagents#39 test labels in the meta-agent workspace, HGM diagnosis sees the private test patch, AHE#15 forgeable best_ever.json, SIA#36 gold answers in the feedback prompt, autoresearch#599 unbound printed metric, pi-autoresearch editable measure.sh). A mount namespace and a hash-bound score receipt would have prevented all seven; all seven issues were filed by outsiders and are unanswered.

The invention gap is much smaller than the adoption gap: PACE (June 2026) already provides a paired anytime-valid commit gate and measures greedy acceptance at 30-42% false commits, and Causal Agent Replay (June 2026) already does full-trajectory counterfactual replay — neither appears in the 58 deep reads and no production loop uses either. The synthesis's claims 2 and 4 (trace cassette) describe things that exist as papers and need integration, not discovery.

Adoption is anti-correlated with gating: the four most-starred loops (ECC 256k, Hermes 244k, autoresearch 95k, OpenViking 37k) have no outcome-based acceptance, while the systems with real gates (SkillOpt, GEPA, Reef, Self-Harness) are 1-3 orders of magnitude smaller. Verification is currently a UX cost the market selects against; a gate will only spread if it is invisible until it blocks something.

SkillOpt is the clearest demonstration that one gate can be both decisive and Goodharted in the same run: the strict held-out gate prevented a 0.554->0.026 collapse ('answer with the document title') while the same optimizer copied judge regexes verbatim into the skill (#154/#175). Drift-protection and scorer-overfitting are different failure classes and need different machinery (held-out gate vs feedback/scorer separation).

'Proposer authors its own test' is a recurring production pattern, not an edge case: EvoMap genes ship their own validation commands ('node --version'), AI-Scientist-v2's agent defines the metric it is judged on, SIA's agent writes evaluate.py (abstention -> 75% reported vs 4.5% real), pi-autoresearch lets the agent decide KEEP, R-Zero/Agent0 use the policy's majority vote as the label. The cheapest fix in the field is 'the harness owns the test'.

Several 'evolved' artifacts never reach the agent at all: EvoMap#624 inject drops strategy text, AutoResearchClaw loads only the first 5 alphabetically sorted skills, Continual Harness logs new components as failures (.id on a str), ECC evolved skills land outside Claude Code discovery paths. An activation probe ('is the promoted thing actually loaded?') would catch more real bugs than a fitness function.

The loops change safety far more reliably than they change capability: memory alone moves refusal 99.4->54.4, 21/21 SkillMisevo configs author unsafe artifacts, carryover ASR doubles — while the same class of loops' capability gains sit within noise (Meta-Harness +1.7pt, HGM 2 tasks of 60, Hyperagents n.s., Self-Harness vs a 3-sentence baseline). A safety canary is therefore both cheaper and higher-signal than most fitness evaluations.

Even the safety literature has the same-model-judges-itself confound: Misevolve's agent trajectories are judged by Gemini-2.5-Pro judging Gemini-2.5-Pro agents; SkillClaw, EvoScientist, AI-Scientist-v2 and R-Zero all score with the generating model's family. Independent-judge spot checks (different family, rubric-blind) are absent across every camp.

Rejected edits are a free labelled negative dataset that almost no one uses: only SkillOpt (rejected-edit buffer) and Reef (max_rejected_history) feed rejections back; GEPA#379 shows the same parent re-proposes identical failed mutations; DGM/HGM archive losers as data but never condition on them. The cheapest sample-efficiency win in the field is also the cheapest anti-churn measure.

RQGM-style evaluator co-evolution, the one principled Goodhart defense, does not fire at practical budgets: the independent OpenRQGM reconstruction saw zero evaluator replacements at 128 outcomes and four at 12,288 (~$25 per expansion). For a small team the actionable defense is scorer-blindness plus independent spot checks, not evaluator evolution.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A1: 'Nobody has a sequential test' is false as invention (PACE/SEA exist) but true as adoption; the contribution is integration + extension.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Ecosystem confirms the adoption half is total: `gh search repos 'anytime-valid agent'` returns zero repos; PACE, SEA, PROCTOR, HackProbe, Blind Curator, TAME all have no public code (rsi_digest scout notes). Every shipped gate in the substrates is a threshold on a mean: Claude Code `claude plugin eval` passes a case when its with-arm mean over 3 runs >= `--threshold` (default 1.0) and exits 1 otherwise — no paired test, and the docs themselves say 'one run tells you little'; agentskills.io's benchmark.json exposes `stddev` but the page notes it is 'only meaningful with multiple runs'; the EEE-compatible xingai-eval-registry ships `diff --fail-on-regression` on raw metrics. OpenClaw's evaluator envelope has a `metrics` map but no decision-rule field. So the integration target is concrete: a PACE-style rule packaged as (a) a `claude plugin eval` grader/threshold replacement, (b) an OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin, (c) a Reef `decide` policy — the three call-sites that already exist and are empty.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A2: 'Nobody does counterfactual replay' is false (CAR, CTA, SkillOpt-Sleep, SkillMisevo-Gym).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Add substrate-native replay primitives the digest missed: Claude Code plugin eval `context.history_file` (continue a saved .jsonl transcript as the next user turn), `evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md` recorded MCP tool answers with `expect:` guards that abort the run with score 0 on input mismatch, and `mock-recordings/` for agent mocks; ModelScope EvalScope's 'Trie agentic trace replay' (2026-05-27) replays real multi-turn agent traces with per-turn token caps and tool-call latency simulation (for perf, not correctness) and its External Agent Bridge (2026-05-22) proxies Claude Code/Codex LLM traffic while recording an `agent_trace`. Replay machinery is now first-party in two vendor toolchains; what is absent everywhere is replay *as a gate on a self-modification*.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A3: The Replay Gap threatens the cassette; correct scoping is regression/behavior-change detector with sandbox-first re-execution and baseline self-divergence as noise model.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The scoping is consistent with what the substrates already expose, which lowers integration risk: plugin eval's MCP mock files are literally 'recorded tool result keyed by (server, tool, input guard)', DSH `tools/post-execute` can `replace` a result and `tools/pre-execute` is a typed Decision, pi `tool_result` can modify, Codex PostToolUse can block/replace. One nuance for section F's '$0.007/replay' number: it is a Claude Code hook-path figure; OpenClaw's Workshop seam is proposal-level (candidate bundle + baseline), not tool-level, so a cassette gate there must run out-of-process and feed its verdict back via `skill_proposal_evaluate` (`decision: block` is the only veto) — the same design, a different attachment point.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A4: 'Camp B is unusable by app developers' is overstated; camps talk (Reef wraps GEPA/SkillClaw/Meta-Harness/SAO); the verification hierarchy explains the camps.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Reef's README (verified 2026-09-14) lists recipes GEPA, Meta-Harness, SAO, SkillClaw, OpenClaw-RL, TTT-Discover, Reefine with measured results on AIME 2025 / Terminal-Bench / WildClawBench, and issue #447 (2026-09-13) converts raw AgentRecords into Harbor tasks — Camp B optimizers are now hot-mountable recipes over a serving proxy. SkillAdam ships as a Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/Copilot plugin; SkillMisevo-Gym adapters wrap Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes native skill-injection paths. The bridge exists; it just carries no acceptance discipline.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A5: Camp B's seven evaluator-integrity leaks are one systems bug; a mount namespace + hash-bound score receipt would have prevented all seven.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The diagnosis holds, but the ecosystem lens changes the prescription: the *receipt* half is already being standardized by people who have never heard of harness evolution. in-toto/attestation #554 'RFC: agent-decision/v0.1 predicate' (open since 2026-05-19, 25 comments, DSSE + Statement v1, cross-implemented by AEP v0.5/WasmAgent and Assay with verdict-parity vectors), IETF draft-farley-acta-signed-receipts (-01 Apr 2026; Ed25519, canonical JSON), OpenSSF Model Signing OMS 1.0 (Sigstore bundle format for multi-file AI artifacts), AI4AI-Bench's host_contract.lock.json and RSI-Exam's sha256-pinned scorer/anchors all exist. None of them has a predicate for 'this candidate artifact was scored by evaluator E on shard D with result R under rule G' — but inventing a fresh receipt format would make it the sixth. The right move is an in-toto predicate/profile that reuses those envelopes, so the receipt is verifiable by tooling that already exists (cosign, Rekor).

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B: per-task regression floor with k-of-n; safety in the gate is the cheapest unclaimed paper; loop-health funnel (activation probe) catches more bugs than a fitness function; evaluator Goodhart = tampering vs overfitting; cross-instance merge open.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Ecosystem data sharpens three of them. (i) Safety-in-gate: the field's de facto safety gate is registry scanning, and the ClawHub Security Signals paper (OpenClaw Foundation + NVIDIA, 67,453 skills) finds VirusTotal, static analysis and SkillSpector overlap on at most 10.4% of combined positives, 0.69% flagged by all three, 81.9% single-scanner — three uncorrelated detectors, none observing the runtime layer; SkillSpector findings 'do not automatically block' on ClawHub and NVIDIA SkillEvaluator is 'advisory only' in Hermes. Behavioral canaries are therefore not competing with an existing gate; they fill a hole the scanners' own authors document. (ii) Activation: Anthropic's plugin-eval docs state 'the most common first finding is a Δ near zero with the case's `tool_used: Skill` grader failing' and mark `tool_used: Skill` graders `scored: false` in two-arm mode — first-party confirmation that activation failure dominates and that activation must be reported separately from effect. (iii) Cross-instance merge: ClawHub signing is 'proposed, not yet implemented' (paper Fig. 1); Hermes Skill Sync is content-addressed (64-hex canonical JSON) but has no re-verification; LobeHub marketplace exposes `isValidated`/`isFeatured` flags, install counts and 1–5 ratings, no evidence.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: C: survey saturation (four shared open problems, no code); adoption anti-correlated with gating so a gate must be invisible until it blocks; five results converge on null effect of LLM-written artifacts; 'proposer authors its own test' is a production pattern; rejected edits unused; spend on evaluation replicates not proposer; cost-normalize against test-time scaling.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree on all counts, with two ecosystem corrections. (1) Anti-correlation has a decisive exception: gates that are registry-side, free to the user and off the hot path spread instantly — ClawHub scans every published skill against VirusTotal and rescans daily since 2026-02-07 at 389k-star scale; OpenClaw Workshop's proposal path shipped in 2026.4.21 and was extended, not removed. 'Invisible until it blocks' is necessary but the stronger predictor is 'someone else pays and it runs at publish/install time'. (2) 'Proposer authors its own test' is now institutionalized by first-party tooling: `claude plugin eval init` has Claude 'propose the cases and graders, try them, and write the files', and agentskills.io's eval workflow has the agent write assertions after seeing its own outputs, with human review as the only check; skill-creator evals explicitly 'do not automatically improve skills'. The field's most-used eval tooling is proposer-authored-test by design, so a gate library must ship graders the proposer cannot edit, not just a statistic. Also: saturation is not only surveys — ≥14 self-evolution benchmarks (SEA-Eval, SEAGym, EvoHarnessBench, HarnessDev, HarnessOpt-Bench, Evo-Bench, PAST-Bench, FinEvo-Bench, EvoAgentBench, GDPevo, RSI-Exam, AI4AI-Bench, SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench) with incompatible protocols and ≥12 bespoke verdict/ledger formats exist; the 15th benchmark or 13th format has negative value.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: D: near-term RSI is harness-first; verification is the bottleneck; nobody ships the verification layer; position the framework as the verification/acceptance layer for harness-RSI.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The positioning is right but 'nobody ships the verification layer' is true only for outcome-based acceptance of self-modifications. Vendors are shipping the adjacent layers now: Anthropic `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269, 2026-09-11) with WITH/W-OUT Δ, `--threshold`, CI exit codes, `schemaVersion: 1` JSON and publishable HTML reports; OpenClaw v2026.8.1 evaluator seam with a documented envelope; NVIDIA SkillEvaluator (440★) + SkillSpector + Skill Cards inside ClawHub and Hermes; Reef's release pipeline with `evaluate`/`decide` policy and canary/shadow routing; ModelScope EvalScope agent traces and bridge. The unoccupied cell is the neutral layer *between* them: an evaluator that registers in every seam, owns the test, emits one comparable record, and decides — not a competitor to plugin eval but its missing decision rule and its cross-harness twin. Positioning against vendor measurement tooling would be crushed; positioning as the record/decision profile they all can emit is adoptable.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: E: 'CI/CD for self-modifying agents' — sealed evaluator + receipts, honest gate library with adapters, safety canary, cassette corpus, loop-health funnel, provenance taint, post-acceptance canary, gate benchmark; killer demo on Claude Code/Hermes; open decisions on language and first adapter.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Components 1–8 are sound; the ecosystem lens reorders and adds. (a) First adapter: Claude Code is right for the builder's data, but the OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` seam is the only substrate contract written *for this exact role* ('external optimization loops') and a GitHub code search (2026-09-14) finds zero non-fork third-party implementations — the first real evaluator there is a visible, low-cost win; and because DSH's hook-protocol runs Claude Code/Codex hooks.json unmodified, one command-hook adapter covers three harnesses. (b) Language: OpenClaw, DSH and pi are TypeScript, Hermes and Reef are Python, Claude Code hooks are language-agnostic — ship the gate as a CLI with JSON stdin/stdout (auto-harness gating.py / hook-protocol shape), not a library in either language. (c) The ledger must be a profile over existing formats (Every Eval Ever record + OTel `gen_ai.evaluation.result` event + in-toto predicate) or it is the 13th bespoke format alongside OpenClaw's envelope, plugin-eval's aggregate-result.json, agentskills' benchmark.json, SEA certificates, agentdescent AcceptDecision, AHE change_manifest, MetaRSI HarnessPatch, RSI-Exam experiment_log, autoresearch results.tsv, Hermes skill_ledger, Reef records, Lin et al. Verdict. (d) The gate benchmark should be packaged as Harbor tasks (13 corpus projects and Reef #447 already speak Harbor; six CLIs are one-line adapters). (e) 'Invisible until it blocks' collides with fail-open seams: OpenClaw evaluator timeouts/errors are 'attributed error outcomes' that do not block, Hermes tiers are advisory, DSH host-only packages activate without approval — the layer must run host-side as its own process and treat 'evaluator unavailable' as reject, as DSH's ApprovalOutcome does. (f) Missing from E entirely: memory artifacts (Claude Code auto memory, Codex memories, Mem0, Cursor Memories — the most-deployed learned artifact, with no seam anywhere except Cursor's human approval) and registry-side evidence (skill hubs). (g) Killer demo: emit a `claude plugin eval`-compatible `aggregate-result.json` so results ride Anthropic's report/Published surface, and a `skill_proposal_evaluate` verdict so OpenClaw users see it in the Workshop board.

gaps.title: A common acceptance record: (candidate digest, incumbent digest, paired evidence, decision rule, verdict, disposition, activation) as a profile over existing standards, not a 13th bespoke format
gaps.description: Every gate in the field writes its own record and none is comparable or verifiable by outside tooling. Adjacent standards cover every neighbor of this cell but not the cell: Every Eval Ever (IBM/EvalEval, arXiv 2606.14516, 114★) standardizes eval *results* with instance-level agentic records and converters for Inspect/HELM/lm-eval; OTel `gen_ai.evaluation.result` (v1.39, still 'Development', moved to its own repo 2026-06-12) carries a score/label/explanation; in-toto `agent-decision/v0.1` (RFC #554) and IETF Acta signed receipts carry tool-call *authorization* decisions; OMS 1.0 signs model artifact bundles. Nothing represents 'artifact X was compared against incumbent Y on paired instances under rule G with evidence E, verdict V, disposition D, and was/was not activated'. The deliverable is a small JSON profile + converters: an EEE record extension (selection denominator, incumbent link, paired outcomes), an OTel event attribute set, and an in-toto predicate so receipts verify with cosign/Rekor; plus emitters for the three call-sites that already have slots (OpenClaw evaluator envelope, plugin-eval aggregate-result.json, Reef decide).
gaps.evidence: ≥12 incompatible formats verified in the digests/docs: OpenClaw `{evaluatorVersion, mode, decision: pass|revise|block, summary, metrics, findings}` (512 KiB cap); Claude Code `aggregate-result.json` `schemaVersion: 1` with `cases[].arms.with/without`, Δ, `partial`/`partialReason`; agentskills.io `evals.json`/`grading.json`/`benchmark.json` (the docs state plugin eval's case format 'is separate from' skill-creator's evals.json — two incompatible first-party formats from one vendor); SEA certificate `{algorithm, round, decision ACCEPT|HOLD|REJECT|NSF, delta_spent, cumulative_delta}`; agentdescent `AcceptDecision{category, reason, p_improve, observed_delta}`; AHE `change_manifest.json` with EFFECTIVE/PARTIALLY_EFFECTIVE/MIXED/INEFFECTIVE/HARMFUL; MetaRSI `HarnessPatch{hypothesis, operations, expected_effect, risks, evidence_refs}`; RSI-Exam `experiment_log.md` rows (version/parent/change/score/kept-or-reverted); karpathy/autoresearch `results.tsv`; Hermes `skill_ledger` JSONL with sha256 before/after; Lin et al. `Verdict{accept, rollback, reason}`; Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance separating verdict (clears/below/inconclusive) from disposition (keep/revert/provisional) with TRACE export. The selection-denominator problem is surfacing independently: xingai-eval-registry (EEE-compatible) added `candidatesCompared`/`candidatesCleared` because 'best-of-2 and best-of-13 look identical in the metrics alone' — the same inflation PACE (30–42% false commits) and RSI-Exam (11.7–24.7% visible→hidden loss) quantify. Reef #357 (2026-09-09, 0 comments) asks for exactly 'what to measure and how to compare results fairly across revisions' with no format named.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: The record falls between four communities that do not meet: supply-chain attestation (in-toto/SLSA/OMS: build provenance and now tool-call authorization), observability (OTel GenAI SIG: scores as events), eval science (EvalEval: benchmark results), and harness-evolution research (each paper's Appendix schema). Each gate author reasonably invents a local schema because none of the four standards has a slot for 'incumbent' or 'decision rule'. Standardization venues that could host it (NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative, Interop Profile due Q4 2026; OTel GenAI SIG) currently have no self-improvement item.
gaps.who_cares: Reef (#357/#358 benchmark spec), OpenClaw Foundation (docs invite external controllers to consume its ledger), Hermes maintainers (#11692 skill-version receipts, P3, resolved by an external 0★ reference integration), EvalEval coalition (EEE converters), auditors and regulated deployers (EU AI Act Art. 12 logging is the stated motivation in in-toto #554), anyone re-analyzing published Camp-B ledgers (Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, SkillOpt rejected buffer, AHE manifests) who today must write seven parsers.

gaps.title: A shared, conformance-tested harness-adapter layer: five groups have each re-written Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes adapters, no third party has ever registered on OpenClaw's evaluator seam, and no one certifies that a seam is fail-closed
gaps.description: The substrates now expose seams for an acceptance layer, but there is no shared adapter library and no conformance suite proving a seam enforces what its docs claim. Deliverable: (1) an adapter matrix (inject artifact / run task / capture trace / read activation / veto) for Claude Code hooks, OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` + `before_tool_call`, DSH `tools/pre-execute`/`post-execute` + hook-protocol, pi `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`resources_discover`, Hermes pending-skills dir + `pre_tool_call`, Codex hooks; (2) a version-pinned conformance suite that answers 'does a deny actually stop the write, does a rejected proposal ever reach disk, does an evaluator timeout fail closed, does a promoted artifact actually load'; (3) a reference evaluator that registers in all of them and emits the gap-1 record.
gaps.evidence: Independent re-implementations of the same adapters: SkillMisevo-Gym adapters for Claude Code `.claude/skills`, Codex AGENTS.md, OpenClaw `.openclaw/skills`, Hermes `.hermes/skills`; SafeEvolve's GovernableStore (5 hook points) 'proven across Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes'; Reef recipes wrapping GEPA/SkillClaw/Meta-Harness; CTA's Hermes adapter PR#2 with a five-check adapter validation; EvalScope External Agent Bridge for Claude Code/Codex; interlinked-cli `hook-support-catalog.json` (176★, surveyed 2026-09-07) — the only cross-harness hook inventory — self-labelled `documented_inventory_not_runtime_certification` with 'presence is documented or declared, not proof that a particular installed version emits or enforces it'. Seam uptake: `gh search code skill_proposal_evaluate` (2026-09-14) returns only OpenClaw docs mirrors and forks (potatoclaw, openclaw-zh, personalclaw, Zeus-Center/Zeus) — zero third-party evaluators ~1.5 months after v2026.8.1 documented the seam 'so external optimization loops can iterate'; of 100 `dsh-plugin` topic repos the only learning-loop plugins are dsh-continual-harness (9★) and dsh-self-improved (12★), neither with a verifier. Fail-open reality the conformance suite must catch: OpenClaw evaluator timeouts/errors are 'recorded as attributed error outcomes' and do not block, default `autonomous.mode: auto` bypasses Workshop entirely; DSH host-only packages activate without approval and 'vm is explicitly not a security boundary'; Hermes write_approval default off, SkillEvaluator tier advisory; Codex 'some specialized tool paths can opt out'; MLAS case study: Hermes Path B persisted 40/40 payloads, OpenClaw blocked 40/40 only via the human queue.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Each vendor documents its own seam and has no incentive to maintain others'; research groups write throwaway adapters for one paper; conformance testing requires version-pinned runs against six fast-moving CLIs (Hermes shipped 947 commits in four days; DSH 14 pre-release tags in 12 days); and nobody has had a fitness signal worth plugging in, so the seams stayed empty.
gaps.who_cares: OpenClaw Foundation and DeepSeek (both explicitly deferred the evaluator to third parties), NVIDIA (SkillEvaluator/SkillSpector need a seam with authority), Reef/CORAL (multi-CLI runners), plugin and skill authors, NIST's Interop Profile work, and every future acceptance-layer paper (SafeEvolve, CTA, SkillMisevo) that currently re-derives the same four adapters.

gaps.title: A gate benchmark packaged on Harbor with released (candidate, evidence, verdict) corpora — the raw material exists but is locked in four unreleased datasets and fourteen incompatible benchmark protocols
gaps.description: The safety lens correctly names 'measure the acceptor's confusion matrix' as a gap; the ecosystem lens adds the distribution mechanism and the missing data. Harbor (laude-institute/harbor, 5.2k★, 1.8k forks) has become the de facto task/verifier format: RSI-Exam, SEAGym, AHE, Self-Harness, Meta-Harness, AI2 'Rethinking', auto-harness, EvoSkill, EvoX, CORAL, Reef (#447 converts raw records into Harbor tasks) and SkillsBench's task layout all run on it, and six CLIs (codex, claude-code, qwen-coder, antigravity, grok-build, kimi-cli) plug in as one-line adapters. A gate benchmark expressed as a Harbor task family (candidate-injection tasks with known-good/neutral/harmful edits and hidden held-out outcomes; result records in EEE format) inherits every adapter and leaderboard instantly. The second half is data: release the ledgers.
gaps.evidence: Unreleased corpora that are exactly the needed ground truth: HarnessDev's 73 frozen harness versions and 26,679 trajectories ('forthcoming'); karpathy/autoresearch's ~700-experiment log (only community results.tsv in #448/#596); EvoHarnessBench runs only through a hosted SDK behind an API key and ngrok; SkillMisevo-Gym code not surfaced; MLAS's 40 CS-* scenarios unreleased; Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl and AHE change_manifest.json exist per run but are not published as datasets. The only registry-scale released verdict corpus is ClawHub Security Signals (67,453 skills with three-scanner evidence + registry verdict) — for security, not effect. Benchmark proliferation without an acceptor metric: SEA-Eval, SEAGym, EvoHarnessBench, HarnessDev, HarnessOpt-Bench (Scale), Evo-Bench, PAST-Bench, FinEvo-Bench, EvoAgentBench, GDPevo, RSI-Exam, AI4AI-Bench, SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench — none scores accept/reject decisions; EvoTrace/EvoReplay's 121-run archive is the one released evolution dataset and covers code evolution only. Reef #358 asks for 'maintained reference tasks and a reproducible evaluation pipeline' with a verifier — an open request from the most likely first adopter.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Papers are rewarded for the agent's score, so ledgers are byproducts nobody curates; benchmark authors each build a protocol (streams, stages, cohorts) tuned to their claim; Harbor is treated as plumbing rather than as the standard it has become; and injecting known-bad candidates needs the accept() call-site, which only Reef/agentdescent/OpenClaw expose.
gaps.who_cares: Reef, agentdescent, auto-harness, Self-Harness, GEPA maintainers choosing a gate; Terminal-Bench/Harbor maintainers (a new task family); AI2/UW and the ICLR RSI workshop reviewers; HarnessDev/EvoTrace authors whose data would become the field's regression corpus; lobehub/wkqdzkd list maintainers who have no 'acceptance' section to point to.

gaps.title: Registries verify malware, not effect: no skill hub, spec or marketplace accepts or displays evidence that a skill helps, and the Agent Skills spec has no field to carry it
gaps.description: Install-time and learned-artifact acceptance are converging on the same object (a SKILL.md bundle) but the registries only run scanners. Deliverable: an `evidence/` convention inside the skill bundle (agentskills.io already documents `evals/evals.json` + `grading.json` + `benchmark.json`; add a signed acceptance record per gap 1 and an activation/uptake field), a registry display contract, and a hub-propagation rule (Hermes Skill Sync, EvoMap Hub, SkillClaw groups, ClawHub) that requires local re-verification before a shared skill goes live.
gaps.evidence: agentskills.io specification (fetched 2026-09-14): frontmatter is `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, free-form `metadata` (string→string), experimental `allowed-tools` — no version, provenance, signature, eval or test fields; validation is `skills-ref validate` (frontmatter syntax only). anthropics/skills (176k★, 20.8k forks): README says skills are 'for demonstration and educational purposes only … always test skills thoroughly in your own environment'; no CONTRIBUTING verification gate. ClawHub: VirusTotal + static + NVIDIA SkillSpector over 67,453 skills; pairwise overlap ≤10.4%, 0.69% triple-flagged, 81.9% single-scanner; SkillSpector advisories do not block; 'signing is proposed, not yet implemented' (paper Fig. 1); Koi's ClawHavoc found 341→824 malicious skills. LobeHub Skills (100k+ skills, targets Claude Code/OpenClaw/Codex/Cursor): install counts, stars, 1–5 ratings, `isValidated`/`isFeatured` flags, no scans or evals documented. ModelScope Skills Center + MS-Agent implement the Agent Skills protocol with no verification. SkillAudit (2606.22613) finds >7% of top-ranked real skills 'at risky status' and proposes utility/cost/safety reports from the package — no registry consumes such a report; the Agent Skills survey (2602.12430) finds 26.1% of community skills vulnerable. Hermes Skill Sync is content-addressed but consent-only; EvoMap Hub validators run the proposer's own commands ('node --version').
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Registries compete on volume and latency (ClawHub rescans daily because scanning is cheap; effect evidence costs model calls); the Agent Skills spec is Anthropic-maintained with a deliberately minimal charter and the eval workflow is documented as author guidance, not as a distributable artifact; scanners are what security vendors sell; and no party owns the question 'did this skill help' as a registry field because the measurement (paired with/without at the consumer's model tier — Lin et al. show benefit is a property of the (skill, consuming agent) pair) is not something a registry can compute centrally.
gaps.who_cares: OpenClaw Foundation and NVIDIA (already co-authoring registry trust papers), LobeHub and ModelScope (marketplaces without a quality signal beyond ratings), Nous (Skill Sync), enterprises installing from 100k-skill catalogs, agentskills.io maintainers, and the SkillAudit/SkillsBench/CoEvoSkills authors whose reports have nowhere to land.

gaps.title: Activation/uptake evidence has no standard representation although six independent efforts now measure it differently
gaps.description: 'Was the artifact loaded, read and followed?' is now computed by at least six projects with six definitions and no shared field, so 'activated' cannot be compared across harnesses or shown in a registry. Deliverable: a minimal activation record (native event → normalized `loaded`/`read`/`followed` with evidence pointer and confidence) attached to the gap-1 acceptance record, with per-harness detectors (Claude Code `Skill` tool_use, Hermes `skill_view`, pi `resources_discover`, DSH `skills/change`, OpenClaw runtime usage receipts), and a tiny benchmark for activation detectors.
gaps.evidence: Lin et al. (2605.30621): skill-load rate 25% vs 96% across consuming agents, adherence drifting .52→.13, SLR/LPR metrics and a rubric-based HFR pipeline. PAST-Bench: a 'mechanism-evidence score' showing identical headline gains with 'artifacts written but never read'. HarnessDev: 18/108 declared mechanisms never fired in 26,679 trajectories; 124/587 writing features dead code. ClawProBench (2608.22510): 'runtime coverage of declared agent configurations' with frozen holdouts. CTA repo replication: 0/34 unnudged with-skill runs read the skill; uptake scoring via distinctive-literal ingestion. Claude Code plugin eval: `tool_used: Skill` grader reported `scored: false` in two-arm mode and the docs' 'most common first finding' is Δ≈0 with that grader failing. OpenClaw Workshop keeps 'runtime usage receipts' and `readSkillHashes`. Production failures the field only found by accident: EvoMap #624 inject drops strategy text; AutoResearchClaw loads only the first 5 alphabetical skills; ECC skills land outside discovery paths; Continual Harness logs new components as failures; Hermes #95976 0 updates for weeks.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Activation is harness-specific (five different native events) and vendors log it in incompatible places (Hermes `.usage.json`, OpenClaw SQLite receipts, Claude Code transcript tool_use, DSH session log); benchmark authors each define it to fit their claim; and registries have no place to show it. The safety lens's 'activation probe' is the mechanism; the missing piece is the comparable record and detector suite.
gaps.who_cares: Plugin/skill authors debugging Δ≈0 (Anthropic's docs make this the first thing to check), PAST-Bench/HarnessDev/ClawProBench authors, the Reliable survey's 'harness-updating vs harness-benefit' agenda, OpenClaw/Hermes maintainers, and anyone building the loop-health funnel.

gaps.title: A portable sealed-evaluator bundle: 'the harness owns the test' has no interoperable packaging, so every substrate re-invents fixtures, mocks and score contracts
gaps.description: The safety lens specifies the mechanism (mount namespace + receipts); this gap is the packaging so one evaluator runs unchanged under Claude Code hooks, OpenClaw's evaluator, a DSH plugin and a Reef recipe. Deliverable: an evaluator bundle spec (image/digest or script + hidden-data digest + score contract + fail-closed wrapper + receipt) modelled on RSI-Exam's two-image boundary and AI4AI-Bench's patch-only boundary, with adapters that surface it as a plugin-eval grader, an OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin, and a Harbor verifier.
gaps.evidence: Divergent existing contracts: RSI-Exam `test.sh` cross-validates `reward.txt`/`reward.json`/`score_details.json`, any exception → 0, sha256 pins on scorer and anchors, network-sealed verifier image; AI4AI-Bench `candidate.patch` as the only crossing artifact, `describe_patch_rejections` pre-GPU static gate, `host_contract.lock.json` protocol identity; Claude Code plugin eval mocks (`evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md` with `expect:` guards; 'a run never starts your plugin's real MCP servers unless you ask'); auto-harness `gating.py` exit 0/1 with gate state agent-writable; PROCTOR 'mechanical rejection overrides LLM approval'; Falsifiable Release Gates (Antahkarana) pre-declared machine-checkable suites; JIT-Agent 'repair only on execution error, never on low score'; EvoMap genes shipping their own validation commands; Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance's own review concluding the gate 'cannot be trusted inside the agent's container' and moving to a host-side shadow audit. Seven Camp-B leaks (DGM#35, HyperAgents#39, HGM, AHE#15, SIA#36, autoresearch#599, pi-autoresearch) all stem from the evaluator living in the proposer's filesystem — a bundle that never mounts there closes them by construction.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Benchmarks build evaluators for their own runner (Harbor, Docker) and substrates build mocks for their own eval tool; the fail-closed wrapper and receipt are 'boring' systems code no paper claims; and there is no consumer for a portable bundle until the adapter layer (gap 2) exists.
gaps.who_cares: RSI-Exam/AI4AI-Bench/SEAGym authors (their verifiers would become reusable), Anthropic plugin-eval users who want a grader the proposer cannot game, OpenClaw evaluator-plugin authors, Reef recipe writers ('representative tasks and an evaluator' is Reef's stated prerequisite), and autoresearch-pattern users (95k+8k+6k stars) whose judge is currently prose-protected.

gaps.title: A cost envelope standard: 'improvement per dollar' cannot be compared because every party reports cost in a different unit, and matched-budget claims are uncheckable
gaps.description: The scientist lens covers the science (search premium vs design premium); this gap is the reporting standard. Deliverable: per-candidate cost fields (proposer tokens, evaluator/judge tokens, replicates, wall-clock, sandbox seconds, list-price estimate) as part of the gap-1 record, with harness-agnostic collection (parse each CLI's own session logs as RSI-Exam's budget.py does) and a matched-budget baseline pointer so an AI2-style test-time-scaling control is a required field, not a paper's courtesy.
gaps.evidence: Incompatible cost reporting: Claude Code plugin eval `COST` is a list-price estimate of model calls with `--max-cost-usd` and `partial: true` semantics; agentskills.io `timing.json` records `total_tokens`/`duration_ms` per run; RSI-Exam budget.py parses codex/claude/gemini/qwen/kimi logs and prints 90/95/99% warnings; AI2 'Rethinking' matches budget in rollouts only, meta-agent and debugger tokens excluded; HarnessDev excludes dev-environment tokens; SEA-Eval shows 31.2× token divergence at similar success; METR expenditure horizon measures $ per 1% speedup; HAL keeps a cost-aware leaderboard; SEA's certificate has `delta_spent` (error budget, not dollars); Meta-Harness ~10M tokens/iteration vs Lin et al.'s finding that a 9B proposer is as good; Reef #357 explicitly asks for 'resource/cost accounting'; the Reliable survey states 'no standardized cost-normalized fitness or reporting format exists'. Hermes users pay ~30K tokens per background review fork with, during #95976, zero yield — a number no tool surfaces.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Cost is borne by the user's API bill, not the framework author; papers report the budget dimension that flatters them; substrates expose tokens in incompatible logs; and no benchmark or registry requires a cost field.
gaps.who_cares: Users of unattended loops (Hermes, SkillOpt-Sleep, OpenViking, autoresearch overnight), reviewers enforcing matched-budget baselines, Reef's benchmark spec, HAL/METR-style leaderboards, and enterprise buyers of 'self-evolving' features.

gaps.title: Memory artifacts have no acceptance seam anywhere: the most-deployed learned artifact (Claude Code auto memory, Codex memories, Mem0, Cursor Memories, Letta MemFS, Hermes MEMORY.md) has no proposal→evaluate→apply contract in any vendor
gaps.description: OpenClaw's Skill Workshop shows what a governed seam looks like for skills; nothing equivalent exists for memory, which is written by more agents than skills and moves safety more reliably (Misevolve: memory alone drops refusal 99.4→54.4%; MemEvoBench). Deliverable: a memory-write proposal contract (entry, provenance/taint, evidence, verdict, activation) and shims that implement it on the existing seams — Claude Code PreToolUse permissionDecision on writes under the memory dir + FileChanged on MEMORY.md, Hermes `memory.write_approval` pending payloads, Mem0's Claude Code plugin hooks, Codex hooks (no memory-specific seam), Letta MemFS git history — plus a memory-specific canary set seeded from MemEvoBench/Misevolve.
gaps.evidence: Claude Code auto memory: Claude decides what to save, 200-line/25KB index, docs say memory is 'context, not enforced configuration'; Codex Memories: two-phase background pipeline into `~/.codex/memories/`, 'a helpful recall layer, not the only source for rules', no approval step; Mem0 (65k★): April-2026 algorithm is single-pass ADD-only, 'memories accumulate; nothing is overwritten', ships as a Claude Code plugin capturing every 5 exchanges; Cursor: human approval before each background memory is saved but 'no diff, no blame, no rollback'; Letta MemFS: git history as the only acceptance; Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md hard-capped with regex injection scanners only; ReasoningBank appends verbatim from a single self-judge; ECC instincts injected into system context with no review; Prime Agent refined prompt notes persist injections. The MLAS matrix rates Cognitive-Resource × Commit as Critical with no mitigation; the 2606.11435 survey warns uncontrolled evolution 'can silently strip existing safety constraints'. No item in either corpus — vendor or research — exposes a memory-level evaluator hook analogous to `skill_proposal_evaluate`.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Memory is treated as UX ('your agent remembers') rather than as a learned artifact; vendors ship it default-on with human audit via /memory as the only control; the artifact is small free text so 'evaluate it' seems disproportionate; and the safety evidence (Misevolve, MemEvoBench) lives in a community that does not ship hooks.
gaps.who_cares: Anthropic/OpenAI/Cursor/Letta/Mem0 (all shipping ungated memory), Hermes/OpenViking users with shared stores, enterprise security teams asking 'which memories came from that injected page' (provenance taint), and the memory-benchmark authors whose findings currently change nothing in deployed products.

gaps.title: No home for the standard: the venues that could adopt an acceptance-record profile (NIST Agent Standards Initiative, OTel GenAI SIG, in-toto attestation WG, EvalEval coalition, agentskills.io) each have an adjacent item and none has a learned-artifact-verification item — and the two vendors positioned to crush it (Anthropic, OpenClaw) are building per-substrate, incompatible pieces
gaps.description: This is a positioning gap rather than a code gap: a small team cannot create a standards body, but it can file a profile in an existing one and get two vendors to emit it. Deliverable: (1) an in-toto predicate proposal for 'artifact-acceptance' filed alongside #554 (reusing DSSE/Statement v1 so cosign/Rekor verify it); (2) an OTel `gen_ai.evaluation.result` attribute extension for incumbent/decision fields; (3) an EEE record profile with selection denominator; (4) PRs adding an optional `evidence`/`version` convention to agentskills.io and to OpenClaw's evaluator envelope; (5) a `claude plugin eval` JSON→record converter. Positioning: Anthropic owns measurement on one substrate (plugin eval, skills spec, 176k★ skills repo) and could add fields to the spec at any time — cooperate by emitting its format; OpenClaw/NVIDIA own registry trust — cooperate via the evaluator seam and Security Signals dataset; DeepSeek deferred its evaluator contract and would adopt a plugin; Nous marked verification 'needs-decision' (#25833, #416 open since March) and accepts external references (#11692); Reef/Human-Agent-Society will adopt a gate + benchmark (#357/#358); ModelScope (EvalScope bridge + Skills Center + AgentEvolver) is the adoption path for the Chinese ecosystem; lobehub (awesome-rsi 164★ with no acceptance section; 100k-skill marketplace) is a distribution channel; OpenAI (Codex memories/skills ungated, no eval command) is the most likely to copy Anthropic's plugin eval rather than adopt a neutral record.
gaps.evidence: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative announced 2026-02-17 (CAISI), three pillars incl. community-led open protocols (MCP named) and 'interoperability evaluation methodologies', first normative output an AI Agent Interoperability Profile in Q4 2026 — no self-improvement item. OTel GenAI conventions: `gen_ai.evaluation.result` event (name, score.value, score.label, explanation) merged Aug 2025, all gen_ai.* moved to a dedicated repo 2026-06-12, still 'Development' with no 1.0. in-toto #554 (open, 25 comments, active cross-implementations AEP v0.5 / Assay / hermes-decision-receipts) scopes 'AI agent authorization decisions', not artifact acceptance. IETF drafts farley-acta-signed-receipts (-01, 2026-04-25) and marques-asqav-compliance-receipts (-08) cover action receipts. EvalEval/IBM Every Eval Ever: schema + datastore + converters (Inspect, HELM, lm-eval), instance-level `agentic` interaction type, no incumbent/decision fields. OpenSSF OMS 1.0 signs multi-file AI artifact bundles (Sigstore bundle format) — usable for skill bundles today, unused by any registry. MCP registry: namespace verification only; 'does not certify that the code is secure … or the runtime behavior will remain unchanged'. Anthropic: two incompatible first-party eval formats; plugin eval reports have a 'Published:' URL surface. lobehub/awesome-rsi: 226 entries, 'no taxonomy node for acceptance gates, promotion/rollback, or verification of self-modifications'.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Standards bodies work on what their members ship — authorization receipts (security vendors), eval results (benchmark labs), observability events (APM vendors); harness-evolution researchers do not attend; vendors have no reason to converge on a neutral record while each substrate's eval tooling is a retention feature; and the field's vocabulary ('RSI') is five weeks old, so no venue has a working-group item yet.
gaps.who_cares: NIST/CAISI Interop Profile authors, OTel GenAI SIG, in-toto maintainers reviewing #554, EvalEval coalition, agentskills.io maintainers, Anthropic DevRel (plugin eval), OpenClaw Foundation, Reef, and every acceptance-layer paper that will otherwise ship its own Appendix schema.

surprising_observations: OpenClaw's `skill_proposal_evaluate` seam — documented in v2026.8.1 with a typed envelope `{evaluatorVersion, mode, decision: pass|revise|block, summary, metrics, findings}`, `correlationId`, `expected_revision_hash`, and prose saying it exists so 'external optimization loops' can iterate — has zero third-party implementations on GitHub as of 2026-09-14 (code search returns only docs mirrors and forks). The single most explicit invitation to build an acceptance layer in a 389k-star substrate has gone unanswered for ~6 weeks; the first real evaluator there is a free, visible win.

Anthropic ships two incompatible first-party eval formats and says so in its own docs: `claude plugin eval` case directories (prompt.md + graders/, `aggregate-result.json` schemaVersion 1) versus skill-creator's `evals/evals.json` + grading.json + benchmark.json — 'Its case format is separate from the evals/evals.json file the skill-creator plugin uses.' Meanwhile the agentskills.io specification has no version, provenance, signature, eval or test field at all (only free-form string `metadata`). The vendor best placed to standardize learned-artifact evidence has not standardized it internally.

The ClawHub Security Signals paper (OpenClaw Foundation + NVIDIA, 67,453 skills) shows the field's de facto safety gate is three near-uncorrelated detectors: pairwise overlap ≤10.4% of combined positives, 0.69% flagged by all three, 81.9% single-scanner, 'none fully observes the runtime layer', and 'signing is proposed, not yet implemented'. The two organizations best positioned to add effect-evidence to a registry already co-author trust-signal research together — and their own conclusion ('layered governance, not single-scanner allow/block') is an argument for a behavioral acceptance layer they have not built.

Attestation standards for agents are moving fast but in the wrong cell for this problem: in-toto #554 `agent-decision/v0.1` (25 comments, cross-implemented by AEP v0.5 and Assay with verdict-parity test vectors), IETF draft-farley-acta-signed-receipts -01, AEP 'action evidence packages', OMS 1.0 for model bundles — all cover tool-call authorization or artifact signing. Hermes #11692 ('receipts for self-improving agents: proving which skill version produced which output') ended in June with an external 0★ reference integration and 'no Hermes core changes requested'. Nobody in any of these threads mentions acceptance of a learned artifact; the predicate is unclaimed.

Harbor has quietly become the substrate standard for harness-evolution research: 13 items across both corpora run on it (RSI-Exam, SEAGym, AHE, Self-Harness, Meta-Harness, AI2 Rethinking, auto-harness, EvoSkill, EvoX, CORAL, Reef, SkillsBench layout), six CLIs are one-line Harbor adapters, and Reef #447 (2026-09-13) converts raw agent records into Harbor tasks. A gate benchmark packaged as a Harbor task family inherits every adapter and every leaderboard — whereas EvoHarnessBench is hosted-SDK-only and HarnessDev's 73 versions / 26,679 trajectories remain unreleased.

IBM/EvalEval's Every Eval Ever (schema + datastore + converters for Inspect, HELM, lm-eval; instance-level `agentic` records with tool_calls, token_usage) is the closest existing evidence format, and a downstream EEE-compatible registry already had to bolt on `candidatesCompared`/`candidatesCleared` because 'best-of-2 and best-of-13 look identical in the metrics alone' — the selection-denominator inflation PACE (30–42% false commits) and RSI-Exam (11.7–24.7% visible→hidden loss) quantify is surfacing independently in registry design. An acceptance-record profile over EEE would land on prepared ground.

Anthropic's plugin-eval documentation independently confirms two of the synthesis's strongest claims: (a) the null/activation finding — 'the most common first finding is a Δ near zero with the case's `tool_used: Skill` grader failing', and the schema separates activation from effect by marking `tool_used: Skill` graders `scored: false` in two-arm mode; (b) the proposer-authors-its-own-test pattern — `claude plugin eval init` has Claude 'propose the cases and graders, try them, and write the files', and the docs advise 'suspect the judge before the plugin' and pinning `--model` so 'a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression'. First-party tooling institutionalizes exactly the failure modes an external gate must own.

ModelScope is the sleeper adopter: EvalScope (3.4k★) already proxies Claude Code and Codex LLM traffic recording a full `agent_trace` (External Agent Bridge, 2026-05-22), replays real agent traces (Trie replay, 2026-05-27), publishes 'evaluation versions' for reproducibility (v1.11.0), runs a Skills Center implementing the Agent Skills protocol, and maintains AgentEvolver — i.e., proxy-point recording, replay, and a skill registry under one vendor-neutral org with no acceptance layer between them.

The 'adoption is anti-correlated with gating' law has a precise exception that tells the builder where to attach: gates spread when they are registry-side, free to the user, and off the hot path. ClawHub scanning every published skill against VirusTotal (with daily rescans) rolled out to a 389k-star ecosystem within weeks of the ClawHavoc incident, and OpenClaw's proposal-first Workshop was extended rather than removed. Gates the user pays for per session (Hermes SkillEvaluator tier, write_approval) default to off or advisory.

Five independent groups have each written their own Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw / Hermes adapter layer for the same purpose — SkillMisevo-Gym (native skill-injection paths), SafeEvolve's GovernableStore (5 hook points), CTA's Hermes adapter (five-check validation), EvalScope's bridge, interlinked-cli's hook-support-catalog (176★, 'documented_inventory_not_runtime_certification') — and none is shared or conformance-tested. The npm-left-pad of this field is a 4-harness adapter package that nobody has published.

Reef (Human-Agent-Society, 1.3k★, pushed 2026-09-14) is the most likely first institutional adopter of an external gate: its harness recipes expose pluggable `evaluate`/`decide` with 'a rejection leaves the previous version serving', its benchmark spec (#357) and reference pipeline (#358) were opened 2026-09-09 with zero comments, its sibling CORAL has open quarantine-gate issues (#67/#124), and it is standardizing on Harbor tasks (#447). One PR could put a PACE-style decide policy and an acceptance record in front of GEPA, Meta-Harness, SkillClaw and SAO simultaneously.

The most-deployed learned artifact has no seam at all: Claude Code auto memory ('context, not enforced configuration'), Codex Memories ('a helpful recall layer'), Mem0 (ADD-only, 'nothing is overwritten', 65k★, Claude Code plugin), Cursor (human approval, 'no diff, no blame, no rollback'), Letta MemFS (git as the only gate). OpenClaw built a governed proposal path for skills; nobody has built one for memory, even though Misevolve shows memory alone moves refusal 99.4→54.4% and the MLAS matrix rates Cognitive-Resource × Commit as Critical with no mitigation.

lens: PRACTITIONER / ADOPTION — someone who runs Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness and Codex daily and asks of every gap "would I install this tomorrow, and would it survive a week without being switched off?" Method: read landscape_digest.md, rsi_digest.md, synthesis_v1.md and both prior gap analyses in full, then mined issue trackers via `gh api` (2026-09-14) for what production users actually file about learned skills/memory: NousResearch/hermes-agent (245k★, 42.8k open issues; 121 issues with 'background review' in the title, 89 with 'curator'), openclaw/openclaw (390k★; Skill Workshop + memory-core dreaming issues), affaan-m/ECC (258k★; continuous-learning-v2), volcengine/OpenViking (37k★; 722 open), EvoMap/evolver (9k★), AMAP-ML/SkillClaw (2.6k★, last push 2026-08-17), deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness (223k★; issues disabled, 6,459 discussions), PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent (20.7k★; issue queue closed 2026-08-15), anthropics/claude-code (145k★; 139 issues titled 'auto memory'), openai/codex (124k★; 26 issues titled 'memories'), microsoft/SkillOpt, tigerless-labs/autoharness, NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution, alchaincyf/darwin-skill. Bodies and comment threads of ~120 issues were read. Throughout, 'user-felt' means a real deployment filed it; 'researcher-only' means no user has asked for it. The constraint 'a gate must be invisible until it blocks something' is taken as a hard adoption requirement and tested against the evidence — with one correction: silent HOLD is as fatal as silent FAIL.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A1 — 'Nobody has a sequential test' is false as invention (PACE/SEA exist) but true as adoption; the contribution is integration + extension (multi-objective, per-task floors, real logs).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, with a practitioner correction on what 'adoption' will look like. Zero user issues across Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Prime, OpenViking, ECC ask for a statistical acceptance test; the one production report that touches it (microsoft/SkillOpt#174: six nights of SkillOpt-Sleep on the user's own skills) says the headline verdict 'was never self-sufficient' and 'the real story only emerged from the per-task diff in evidence.jsonl'. Users who build their own loops independently converge on the same discipline PACE formalizes — hermes-agent#96704 (jimy-r): 'single-run comparisons kept lying to us... every case now replays 3 to 5 times and reports a pass rate with stddev, never one number'; AfshinMirhamed in the same thread proposes an eligible->activated->adhered->effective chain. So the sequential test will be adopted only if it is packaged as the per-task diff table users already read, with the e-process as the invisible stop rule behind it. The extension that matters most for users is the tri-state outcome SkillOpt maintainers demanded in #155 (pass/fail/inconclusive for timeouts and budget caps), which PACE's binary paired design does not have.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A2 — 'Nobody does counterfactual replay' is false (Causal Agent Replay, CTA, SkillOpt-Sleep tool-aware replay, SkillMisevo clean-session replay).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, and add that production users are already asking for exactly the sandbox-first replay the synthesis converges on: microsoft/SkillOpt#155 (2026-07-19, open) 'AgenticReplayBackend — replay mined tasks with a real agentic CLI in a throwaway worktree, gate on the diff'; Microsoft maintainers endorsed it 2026-07-21 and 2026-08-07 with three constraints the synthesis should adopt verbatim: a git worktree is 'disposable state, not a security boundary' so real execution needs a container with isolated credentials/config/network; outcomes must be pass/fail/inconclusive; agent execution disabled by default. hermes-agent#107914 (2026-09-11) requests 'environment-probing background review — verify uncertain memory/skill writes against the live environment before committing', citing arXiv 2609.11060 (Microsoft, Sep 10 2026), which neither digest contains. DSH's plugin marketplace already hosts dsh-verify ('agents self-test and pass, real browsers tell the truth'), dsh-verification ('claimed-done becomes actually-done'), dsh-llm-verifier and a 'self-optimizing-plugin' loop example — verification is being built as third-party plugins on the largest substrate, in the slot the synthesis targets.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A3 — The Replay Gap means a cassette is a regression/behavior-change detector, not a fitness function; scope = baseline self-divergence, prefix-valid counterfactuals, sandbox re-execution on divergence.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The scoping is right but the practitioner data says the first thing a cassette must measure sits upstream of divergence: whether the artifact reached the model at all. Users file this constantly and nothing measures it: anthropics/claude-code#82056 (48 comments, 2026-07-28) 'a session cannot determine whether its auto-memory index loaded whole, truncated, or not at all' — three indistinguishable failure modes plus a fourth (store slug not stable across versions) discovered in-thread; #92998 (re-filed after five prior reports were closed by the stale bot) MEMORY.md overflow silently discards the NEWEST entries so corrections are lost while the text they correct stays loaded; #90604 a user-authored safety rule was invisible because the memory block was sourced from the wrong cache directory; openai/codex#29033 memories generated locally but never injected into new threads; PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent#819/#1891 the harness overview is an alphabetical 6-entry head slice — measured 22/28 prompt notes and 63/69 memories never entered context in any session; EvoMap/evolver#624 inject drops the strategy text; hermes-agent#110402 agent ran 11 image generations ignoring a loaded skill's explicit rule; CTA's own replication found 0/34 unnudged with-skill runs read the skill. So a cassette's cheapest and highest-yield output is an activation/adherence receipt per session (which needs no re-execution and no LLM call), and divergence measurement is the second product. The synthesis's section F confirms pure VCR is dead, which matches: users do not want replayed outcomes, they want to know what loaded and what changed.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A4 — 'Camp B is unusable by app developers' was overstated; GEPA/DSPy and SkillOpt-Sleep are usable and the camps do talk (Reef wraps GEPA/SkillClaw/Meta-Harness).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Usable is not used. The one first-party attempt to graft Camp B onto a production Camp A harness — NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution (5.3k★, GEPA/DSPy over SKILL.md) — is stalled with 123 open issues: #141 'skill evolution is a no-op: optimized_module.skill_text is the unchanged baseline', #11/#34/#74/#93/#110 the constraint validator rejects every evolved skill (validates body without frontmatter), #119 'optimization works but evolved file is never deployed', #37 'project appears stalled — 19 PRs pending', #18 (r=6) 'is this integrated into hermes-agent?' (it is not); last push 2026-06-17. Hermes users asked for SkillOpt integration (hermes-agent#32925, r=13, 2026-05-27) and nothing shipped. SkillClaw — the Reef-style proxy that 'talks' to Hermes/OpenClaw/Codex — has issues titled 'Broke the Harness' (#61), 'Unauthorized Config Mutation' (#71, edited an unrelated Hermes profile), '弃用，侵入式干扰codex正常执行' (#35, deprecated: intrusively interferes with Codex), and '是要烂尾了？' (#89, is it abandoned?); last push 2026-08-17. The camps talk at the API level and break at the plumbing level (discovery paths, frontmatter validators, deploy step, proxy protocol). For a third-party gate this means the adapter layer, not the gate algorithm, is where adoption is won or lost.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: A5 — Camp B's evaluator-integrity failures are one bug (proposer's filesystem view includes the evaluator); a mount namespace + hash-bound receipt fixes all seven.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, and the same single bug has a Camp A twin that users have already named: the write gate is a convention on one tool, not a boundary on the file path. hermes-agent#99729 (2026-08-31): 'skill_manage's approval gate is a convention, not an enforced boundary — write_file/patch/terminal reach ~/.hermes/skills/ directly'; #105921 (2026-09-08 incident): the skill-review fork held the whole memory toolset and deleted four standing permission rules from MEMORY.md, nothing surfaced it; #107850/#108032 write_origin not set on the same-session injection turn, external_dirs skills misclassified as agent-owned so guards do not fire; gfpyc's production report in #96704: a background fork rewrote a working, user-validated chrome-devtools skill at 02:17 'with no ledger entry (the review writes files directly, bypassing skill_manage bookkeeping)' — the corrupted rule nearly caused the agent to kill the user's everyday Chrome. OpenClaw's Workshop docs concede direct maintenance in auto mode 'does not create proposals, run a post-turn scanner, or record automatic rollback snapshots', and openclaw#100071 shows a workspace skill silently shadowing a reviewed plugin skill of the same name. anthropics/claude-code#85597: two concurrent sessions sharing ~/.claude silently overwrite each other's memory. The generalization of the mount-namespace fix: the gate must intercept the generic file-write path to the learned-state tree (any tool, any thread, any harness), or it is prose.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B claim 3 — Per-task regression floor: agree, with k-of-n confirmation because a floor at n=2 is noise.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree; SkillOpt#174 is the canonical user report (val=4 tasks, aggregate 0.682->0.852 accepted while essay_wl2 regressed 0.91->0.82 and nothing improved). Two practitioner caveats on k-of-n: (1) users will not pay for confirmation replays — darwin-skill#25 asks how to reduce the token cost of evaluating one skill; claude-code#71633 reports skill-creator's eval loop 'burns ~50% of a usage window in minutes'; Codex users disabled Memories because background generation drained their weekly quota while idle (codex#19105, #18699, #19732) — so the floor must ride on evaluations the user already ran (their own test runs recorded by hooks), not on new rollouts; (2) the floor's product form is the per-task diff table plus 'protected' status on tasks with observed stability, which is what #174's author derived by hand from evidence.jsonl. Hermes users independently protect artifacts rather than tasks: hermes-agent#41939 (r=8) shipped `.protected` dotfile markers after an agent 'aggressively rewrote' a skill representing weeks of work.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B claim 4 — Safety inside the gate is the cheapest unclaimed paper; loops change safety more reliably than capability; 30–100 domain-conditioned canary prompts per candidate.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree that no gate has a safety term; disagree on which safety. No user issue in any tracker reports refusal-rate decay. The safety incidents users file are operational: hermes-agent#6051 'learned helplessness' (transient Playwright failure persisted as durable tool-avoidance guidance); #101351 background review persisted a plaintext GitHub PAT into .git/config and API keys into session captures; #105921 review deleted four permission rules; gfpyc/#96704 corrupted skill nearly destroyed the user's browser session; openclaw#84882 memory-core Dreaming silently deleted 46 daily memory files (discovered post hoc from evidence); openclaw#8776 (r=11) bundled soul-evil hook lets an injected agent swap its own system prompt via config.patch; openai/codex#41711 'PRIVATE CHAT THREAD EXFILTRATION' — the memory writer sent local-provider transcripts to OpenAI; EvoMap/evolver#198 git reset --hard in the wrong directory lost 3,711 files; claude-code#71525 a stale memory note was treated by the auto-mode classifier as a standing authorization boundary; #85264 a fork subagent fabricated a completion report and wrote false claims into persistent memory. A domain-conditioned canary that users would keep on is therefore: destructive-action, credential/secret persistence, cross-provider/cross-user egress, and 'rule contradicts the environment' probes run against the user's own environment — HarmBench-style refusal probes are a researcher-only signal for this audience. The paper is still cheap; its canary set should be seeded from these incident classes (MLAS's 40 CS-* scenarios are unreleased).

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B claim 5 — Loop-health telemetry: the flagship Hermes loop was killed by two safety guards interacting; several 'evolved' artifacts never reach the agent; an activation probe would catch more real bugs than a fitness function.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, and this is by a wide margin the most user-felt gap. Additional confirmed silent-failure incidents beyond the synthesis's list: hermes-agent#83260 a failed curator LLM call is recorded as 'no change' (success and non-execution indistinguishable); #103235 completion log reports result=none for patch and write_file because the prefix classifier misses the tool's message format; #105770 both write_approval switches on for ~8 weeks accumulated 77 pending memory writes and 164 pending skill writes with no visible signal; #87250 background-review token usage invisible to telemetry; #90683 post-turn review runs as a daemon thread and CLI/kanban exit kills it mid-request every run; #109375 reviews lost in short-lived runtimes; affaan-m/ECC#2370/#2417 observer archives observations as processed even when analysis fails (one failed run consumed 3,073 observations), #2746 observations routed to global scope on missing cwd, #1231 instincts stored but never injected (closed 2026-04); openai/codex#26684 consolidation silently drops or duplicates memories under concurrent saves; #17490 no stage-1 outputs because imported threads keep has_user_event=0; volcengine/OpenViking#4960 malformed custom template silently overrides the built-in and breaks the whole agent-evolution pipeline with no UI/API error, #4655 skill extraction is a no-op under a documented flag; PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent#792 auto-refine never fires under -p, #1208 '/refine self-improvement is invisible — users cannot tell what changed or that it even ran' (closed unfixed when Prime closed its issue queue 2026-08-15). The funnel's four counters should be joined by a fifth: 'ran' vs 'reported ran'.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B claim 6 — Evaluator Goodhart splits into tampering (sealed evaluator) vs overfitting via feedback (scorer-blind channel, mutation-content scan, independent-judge spot checks).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree. Practitioner addition: the overfitting class is experienced by users as the optimizer fighting their own conventions — SkillOpt#175: the heading regex rejects numbered/bilingual headings so 'the optimizer fixes it by forbidding the skill's own heading format'; #154: intent-level improvements are 'dropped or Goodharted into shallow proxy rules'. And a third class the synthesis does not name: the security scanner Goodharting the human — hermes-agent#94353 a staged skill that quotes an injection-pattern phrase in prose cannot be approved at all ('scanner-refused writes cannot be human-approved'), leaving 'only one way forward: bypassing both the security scan and the approval gate by writing the files directly'; #109536 typosquat check flags Python builtins (74 HIGH findings in one file); autoharness#162 obfuscation patterns flag legitimate Python. False positives without an override path convert a gate into a bypass incentive — a gate benchmark should report false-block rate on the user's own benign edits as a first-class metric.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: B claim 7 — Cross-instance merge with verification does not exist; Byzantine-robust aggregation of text artifacts is genuinely open.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The research problem is real but it is not where users bleed first. Merge conflicts show up inside one machine before any federation: gfpyc/#96704 failure mode 5 — the foreground agent patched a stale snapshot while the background review had rewritten the same file minutes earlier (skill_view returned a dedup stub), producing 'a blend of two writers' intent'; claude-code#85597 two concurrent sessions overwrite each other's memory files; openclaw#65374 memory-core dreaming pools all agents' sessions into one corpus and synthesizes first-person narratives from other agents' memories; hermes-agent#1780 `hermes skills update` clobbers agent-adapted skills on provider updates; #75317 curator consolidation destroys cross-profile sharing. Users' cross-user worry is privacy, not Byzantine robustness: SkillClaw#11 'will User A indirectly obtain User B's personal information, work habits, or environmental preferences?'; codex#41711 provider-boundary exfiltration. So the merge protocol's first deliverable is a three-writer ownership model (user / foreground agent / background reviewer+curator / updater) with per-writer authority, before quarantine of remote contributions.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: C — Adoption is anti-correlated with gating; a gate will only spread if it is invisible until it blocks something.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, with a sharpening the issue data forces: invisibility must be one-sided. Evidence for the constraint: OpenClaw shipped a full proposal-gated Workshop and flipped its default to ungoverned `auto`; Hermes `write_approval` and `guard_agent_created` default off (#16461 open since April); Codex users turn off memories for quota (#19105/#19732); Hermes users ask to suppress the loop's notifications (#46908, #30970); claude-code#91188 (52 comments) is about a compaction nag; claude-code#71633 and darwin-skill#25 are about eval cost. Evidence for the sharpening: when the gate IS invisible in the wrong direction it starves silently and users bypass it — hermes-agent#105770 (241 staged writes unnoticed for 8 weeks; 'stale pending items drift out of sync... several are already un-applyable'), #76795 (queue grows unbounded, newest last), #94353 (deadlock -> direct writes), #98330 (desktop has no review surface at all), openclaw#109278 (70-second approval window visible only to a paired admin UI), #91266 (apply times out because approval wait exceeds the tool watchdog), #101657 (quarantined proposals are dead-ends). The rule is: silent on pass, loud on block, and never silent on hold — a held item must expire or escalate. A gate that adds any recurring cost or notification on the pass path will be disabled within a week; a gate that blocks without an override path will be routed around within a day.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: C — Five results converge on near-zero causal effect of LLM-written artifacts; a null-effect audit of production stores is cheap and high impact; a gate that rejects most edits 'for free' is correct behavior.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Agree, and users are asking for the audit themselves: hermes-agent#96704 (2026-08-27, open) 'RFC: add evals/skills/, a paired-arm harness measuring whether agent-written skills actually help' — 'there is no answer, today, to does a skill written by the background review make the next session better, worse, or neither'; the thread designed three arms and notes the cheapest (activation from transcripts) 'needs no model runs and could produce numbers within a day'. Production data posted in that thread (4-agent deployment, 182 skills, 2026-06-12 to 08-29): several agent-created skills with use_count=0 weeks after creation; three clusters of 3 same-topic skills created within 6–8 hours with zero references; a 544-line mainstay skill whose 199-char description truncates to zero trigger words in the ~57-char matcher window (its 60 uses came from agents knowing it by name); a proposal persisted as a skill ~10 seconds after being submitted for human review. claude-code#75334: users count '4 to 6 identical corrections per data type' across sessions despite memory files; #76408 closed 2026-09-03 without fix; codex#24172 'memories are forgotten'. The correct-behavior framing needs one caveat from #89963: 'half of what the fork produced for us is genuinely good' — users will not accept a gate that rejects everything, so the report must separate 'rejected as no-op' from 'rejected as harmful', and 'no-op' should cost nothing.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: C — 'Proposer authors its own test' recurs; the harness owns the test. Rejected edits are a free negative dataset. Spend on evaluation replicates with a cheap proposer (Lin et al.); cost-normalize against test-time scaling (AI2).
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Harness-owns-the-test: agree, user-visible in EvoMap (genes validate with `node --version`; auto-filed '[Auto] Recurring failure: Repeated failures with gene' issues #534/#577/#530/#466 show the loop banning its own genes) and in hermes-agent#89963 where the background reviewer labelled placeholder text (NNN/HH:MM) as 'Verified 2026-08-04' and codified a helper script that never existed, which later 'halted a production run'.
