Rejected-edit reuse: no user asks for it; researcher-only. Cheap proposer: partially — the user-side cost problem is not proposer strength but the loop's fixed overhead: Hermes ~30K tokens per review event, #93057 same-model review replays 350k–384k of context repeatedly because compaction is disabled, #90446 refusal loops re-send the full context up to 16 times, #99661 13+ nudge firings in one session; OpenViking#505 O(n²) semantic reprocessing per stored memory, #4578 bulk ingestion starves interactive commits 'for days'; DSH discussion #6574 one 'learn this zip' request fanned out to 146 subagent sessions and 343M cache-read tokens (62% of the user's entire history) because breadth has no cap. AI2 cost-normalization: agree but researcher-only; users want a per-loop spend meter, not a matched-budget baseline.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: D — Position the framework as the verification/acceptance layer for harness-RSI: 'my agent modified itself' becomes 'tested, gated, activated, attributed, revertible'.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The function is right; the word is wrong for adoption. No user issue across ten trackers uses 'RSI' or 'self-improvement verification'; the vocabulary users use is version control, receipts, diff, undo, budget. The highest-reaction learning-loop-adjacent issue in Hermes is #12238 (r=38, 2026-04-18) 'Built-in Automatic Backup & Version Control for Agent Data (~/.hermes/)' — 'track how their agent evolved over time'; hermes-agent#11692 asks for receipts 'proving which skill version produced which output'; codex#34668 wants 'a visible write receipt'; codex#30299 wants CLI commands to 'inspect, prune, delete, and scope' a 4,896-line/601KB MEMORY.md; prime-agent#684 wants the diff before apply; openclaw#103871 wants preview before approval; claude-code#78398 wants a batched promote/keep/discard adjudication step. The five verbs in the thesis (tested, gated, activated, attributed, revertible) map exactly onto what users ask for, in reverse priority order: revertible and activated are demanded now, attributed is being requested (#96704), gated is tolerated if invisible, tested is the paper. Ship as 'git + CI for the state your agent writes to itself'; reserve 'verification layer for harness-RSI' for the ICLR-workshop framing — both audiences are real and the same code serves them.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: E — Design thesis 'CI/CD for self-modifying agents' with 8 components (sealed evaluator, statistical gate, safety canary, cassette corpus, loop-health funnel, provenance taint, canary+auto-revert, gate benchmark) and the overnight-report killer demo.
hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: The demo is the right artifact — it answers Prime#1208, claude-code#82056 and hermes#105770 in one screen — but three things are missing and the component order is inverted for adoption. Missing: (a) an undo primitive that actually restores — hermes-agent#96962 curator rollback restores SKILL.md but not references/scripts, #83580 51 of 62 archived skills unrecoverable via the documented CLI, #75228 rollback nests the skill inside itself, OpenViking#4178 (2026-08-21) asks for one-click reversal of a session's entire memory impact from memory_diff.json and lists the hazard (later sessions modified the same memory), claude-code#92998 overflow drops the newest entries with no record of what was dropped; (b) an ownership/write-authority model so user-validated artifacts are immutable to background writers by default (hermes#41939, gfpyc failure mode 8: 'review writes to existing, user-validated skills must require human approval'); (c) interception of the generic file-write path across harnesses, not adapters to eight gate call-sites (hermes#99729; OpenClaw's own admission that its gate only functions where the runtime honors a rooted file surface). Order by user demand from the issue corpus: 5 (funnel + activation) > 7 (revert, depth>1, verified restore) > 6 (provenance, incl. Hermes#89963 'Verified' semantics and claude-code#87783 'claims but not observations') > 4 (cassette, but tri-state per SkillOpt#155) > 2 (statistical gate, hidden) > 3 (canary, reframed to destructive/credential/egress) > 1 (sealed evaluator: Camp B only) > 8 (gate benchmark: researcher-only). The demo line '1 never activated — here's why' is the sentence that sells it; add '3 reverted with one command' and 'cost of all of this: $0.42' — the corpus shows a loop that does not print its own cost gets disabled.

gaps.title: A change feed with receipts for everything the agent writes to itself ('what changed since yesterday, from which session, and why')
gaps.description: Every harness stores self-modifications in a different, unrendered place (Hermes skill_ledger JSONL + .usage.json, OpenClaw SQLite event ledger, Prime refinements.jsonl, Codex stage1_outputs SQLite + MEMORY.md, Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory with no log at all, ECC observations.jsonl, OpenViking memory_diff.json per commit) and none of them shows the user a diff feed: which artifact changed, the before/after, the originating session and evidence, and a content hash tying it to later sessions. Users discover changes only by grepping directories or when something breaks. The primitive is a content-addressed watcher over the learned-state trees of all installed harnesses that emits one record per write (who: user / foreground agent / background reviewer / curator / updater; what: hash before/after; from: session id + evidence pointer) and renders 'diff since <time>' and 'history of <artifact>' — the git log the synthesis's overnight report is built on.
gaps.evidence: PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent#1208 '/refine self-improvement is invisible — users cannot tell what changed or that it even ran' (two users on one team concluded there is no self-improvement; closed unfixed 2026-08-15 when the issue queue was closed) and #684 'show refine.run() diff before applying'. NousResearch/hermes-agent#12238 (r=38) backup & version control for ~/.hermes to 'track how their agent evolved over time'; #18402 'hermes update should show what changed'; #11692 'receipts for self-improving agents: proving which skill version produced which output' (14 comments); #87250 review-fork token usage invisible; #105770 241 staged writes unnoticed for 8 weeks; #99704 diff preview renders empty for patch-type items. openai/codex#30299 no CLI to inspect/prune/delete a 4,896-line MEMORY.md; #34668 'explicit, auditable promotion... with a visible write receipt'. anthropics/claude-code#82056 (48 comments) load receipts; #78398 batched adjudication; #92998 overflow silently discards newest entries. openclaw/openclaw#103871 preview before approval; #109278 approval succeeded but operator list/replay empty. volcengine/OpenViking#4178 needs the per-session diff to reverse a session's memory impact. gfpyc (hermes#96704): a working skill was rewritten at 02:17 'with no ledger entry'.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Each harness team owns only its own store and treats the ledger as internal telemetry (Hermes explicitly: 'telemetry, not a gate'); Claude Code and Codex memory are first-party features with no external diff surface; a cross-harness feed is nobody's product because it lives in the user's home directory rather than in any one repo. It also looks too trivial to publish and too unglamorous to fund, yet it is the prerequisite for every gate, attribution and rollback feature in the synthesis.
gaps.who_cares: Every daily user of Claude Code auto-memory, Hermes background review, OpenClaw Workshop/dreaming, Codex Memories, Prime /refine (collectively ~1M GitHub stars of harnesses); team leads who need to answer 'which learned rule caused that'; the gate benchmark (a ledger is its input format).

gaps.title: Session-level load and adherence receipts: did the artifact reach the model, complete or truncated, and did the session act consistently with it
gaps.description: A harness-side (not loop-side) receipt emitted per session for every persistent artifact: resolved store identity + hash, bytes/lines available vs loaded, status complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store, and — from the session transcript — whether loaded rules were followed or contradicted by tool calls. Distinct from the loop-health funnel (loop counters and alarms): this works with no learning loop at all, for hand-written CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/MEMORY.md, which is 100% of Claude Code users, and it is the cheapest arm of the null-effect audit (activation from transcripts, no model calls). The Lin et al. finding that benefit depends on activation (25% vs 96% skill-load rate) and adherence drift (.89->.80 vs .52->.13) is the research statement of the same gap.
gaps.evidence: anthropics/claude-code#82056 (48 comments, open): three indistinguishable failure modes (index truncated / not read / written to a different store) plus a fourth found in-thread (project slug unstable across versions for paths with underscores); #92998 newest entries silently discarded; #90604 safety rule missed because the memory block came from the wrong cache path; #81833 inconsistent loading across git worktrees; #75334/#76408 memory acknowledged but not applied ('4 to 6 identical corrections per data type'); #92750/#87613 subagents receive memory contrary to docs (34% of a small subagent's payload). openai/codex#29033 memories generated but never injected; #24172 'memories are forgotten'; #22187 injected by CLI but not by Windows app with same CODEX_HOME. PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent#819/#1891: 22/28 prompt notes and 63/69 memories never entered any session's context (alphabetical head slice). affaan-m/ECC#1231 instincts never injected; EvoMap/evolver#624 strategy text dropped at inject; AutoResearchClaw loads first 5 alphabetical skills. NousResearch/hermes-agent#110402 agent ignored loaded skill for 11 consecutive generations; gfpyc/#96704 a 544-line mainstay skill is invisible to the ~57-char trigger window. CTA replication: 0/34 unnudged with-skill runs read the skill. PAST-Bench: identical headline gains 'can come from unintended pathways (artifacts written but never read)'.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Harnesses log what they injected into the system prompt but not as a user-readable receipt, and none reconciles 'loaded' with 'followed'; adherence checking needs a per-artifact rule extraction that nobody wants to pay an LLM for per session (Lin et al.'s HFR pipeline does it offline). Claude Code's /context and InstructionsLoaded hook report which files loaded but not completeness (per #82056 thread); the truncation warning is injected into the model's context, not shown to the user. Session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl, Hermes sessions, Codex rollouts) contain everything needed, so this is a parser, not a research problem.
gaps.who_cares: Claude Code users with large MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md (heavy-scale report #83114: 1,200+ memory files, index pinned at cap for weeks); Hermes deployments with 100+ skills (#13534: 146 skills); Codex Memories users; the paired-arm eval effort in hermes#96704 (it names eligible->activated->adhered->effective as the chain); anyone whose gate needs to distinguish 'no effect' from 'never loaded'.

gaps.title: Ownership and write-authority for learned artifacts: which writer may mutate which artifact, enforced on the file path rather than on one tool
gaps.description: Every production loop has at least four writers of the same files — the user, the foreground agent, an unattended background reviewer/curator/dreaming job, and the package updater — and no harness has an ownership model beyond a per-skill opt-in pin. Needed: per-artifact authority (user-validated artifacts immutable to unattended writers by default; agent-created artifacts patchable by the loop; updater may not clobber locally adapted artifacts without a merge), provenance of the write origin carried across threads and subagents, enforcement at the path level for any tool (write_file, patch, shell redirection, subagent) and any harness sharing the directory, and a conflict check (hash-at-read vs hash-at-write) so two writers cannot interleave. This is the Camp A twin of the sealed-evaluator boundary: the seven Camp B leaks were 'proposer sees the evaluator'; the Camp A incidents are 'unattended writer reaches user-owned state'.
gaps.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent#41939 (r=8): agent 'aggressively rewrote' a skill representing weeks of work; fixed only by an opt-in `.protected` dotfile (PR #42223). #99729: 'skill_manage's approval gate is a convention, not an enforced boundary — write_file/patch/terminal reach ~/.hermes/skills/ directly'. #105921 (incident 2026-09-08): a skill-triggered review held memory remove/replace and deleted four standing permission rules. #107850/#108032: write_origin unset on injection turns; external_dirs skills misclassified as agent-owned. #1780: `hermes skills update` reinstalls upstream over agent-adapted skills. #89963: pinning is displaced — 'pin gates a name, the loop selects a place' (codification landed in an unpinned sibling within hours). gfpyc/#96704 failure modes 5 and 8: stale-snapshot concurrent edit; validated skill mutated at 02:17 with no ledger entry, nearly killing the user's Chrome. openclaw/openclaw#100071: workspace (agent-writable) skills silently shadow reviewed plugin skills of the same name; #107707: Workshop apply overwrites a live skill with plan text verbatim (data loss); default `autonomous.mode: auto` bypasses the Workshop entirely. anthropics/claude-code#85597: two concurrent sessions silently overwrite each other's memory/rule files; #85264: a fork subagent wrote false claims into persistent memory; #82184: auto-memory outranks project instructions. affaan-m/ECC#2746: observations routed to the wrong (global) scope. SkillClaw#71: setup edited an unrelated Hermes profile's config.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Harness authors add guards per incident inside one tool (Hermes has six guards in skill_manager_guards.py, all bypassable by write_file) because a path-level boundary requires a mount/permission layer they do not control; OpenClaw's rooted write surface only works in its embedded runner; Claude Code exposes PreToolUse permissionDecision on the memory dir (usable) but nothing equivalent exists across harnesses; provenance ContextVars are lost across worker threads (hermes#79004/#88053/#94324 — the same bug fixed three times). Nobody has defined the ownership vocabulary (user-validated / agent-created / bundled / imported / adapted) as a cross-harness contract.
gaps.who_cares: Anyone who has hand-built a skill and runs an unattended loop (Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex Memories, Claude Code auto-memory); multi-agent single-machine setups (openclaw#65374 dreaming identity contamination); teams sharing stores; the safety canary (most destructive incidents are unauthorized mutations of good artifacts, not authored bad ones).

gaps.title: Undo that actually restores: session-scoped and artifact-scoped rollback with depth >1 and verified round-trip
gaps.description: The safety lens covers when to trigger a revert; this gap is the mechanism users lack. Requirements from incidents: snapshot the whole learned-state tree (skill dir including references/scripts/assets, memory files, index files) content-addressed before every unattended write; expose 'undo everything session X did' (adds -> delete, updates -> restore before-content, deletes -> recreate) with a conflict check for artifacts touched by later sessions; expose 'restore artifact Y to version N'; test each snapshot by round-tripping before trusting it; retain depth >1 and GC by policy. Today rollback exists as a feature name in Hermes, OpenClaw and OpenViking and fails in the field.
gaps.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent#96962: curator rollback restores SKILL.md but not references/scripts — 'rollback is not a full restore'; #83580: 51 of 62 archived skills unrecoverable via the documented CLI (the curator prompt tells the model to `mv` with a naming scheme restore() rejects); #75228: rollback 'reports state restored' but nests the skill inside itself; #109331: backup creates a snapshot its own rollback rejects on absolute symlinks; #91449: backup snapshot recursively inflates to 24GB and hangs startup; #107539: ledger blobs grow unbounded with no GC. openclaw/openclaw#84882: Dreaming silently deleted 46 daily memory files, discovered days later from evidence; #107707: 'git recovery is not guaranteed'; #101657: quarantined proposals have no path back. volcengine/OpenViking#4178 (2026-08-21): one-click reversal of a session's memory impact is done by hand from memory_diff.json 'many times... error-prone' and must detect later modification by other sessions. anthropics/claude-code#92998: overflow discards newest entries with no record of what was lost; openai/codex#26684: consolidation drops/duplicates memories; #9203 (r=493) 'please make /undo back'. EvoMap/evolver#198: `git reset --hard` in the wrong root lost 3,711 files.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Each store has its own layout and rollback is implemented as a per-tool feature (skill_manage rollback_entry, Workshop rollback metadata, OpenViking memory_diff) rather than as a snapshot of the tree, so support files, index lines and cross-artifact effects are missed; git is the obvious substrate but the trees live outside repos (~/.hermes, ~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/memories, ~/.openclaw) and users do not want a second git workflow; nobody tests restore paths (three Hermes rollback bugs were found by users doing a rollback for real).
gaps.who_cares: Every user who has lost a skill or memory to an unattended writer; OpenViking enterprise operators (#4178 is a real-environment request); the post-acceptance auto-revert design (needs a working undo to call); the overnight-report demo ('3 reverted with one command').

gaps.title: A spend ledger and budget caps for the learning loop and for the gate itself
gaps.description: Users disable any self-improvement mechanism whose cost they cannot see or bound. Needed: per-loop accounting (tokens, cache reads, wall-clock, API dollars) attributed to background review / curation / consolidation / replay / gate evaluation, read from each harness's own session logs (the RSI-Exam budget.py pattern), a per-day cap with a circuit breaker on repeated refusals or identical retries, breadth caps on subagent fan-out, and a line in every report stating what the gate cost. The scientist lens's cost-normalized accounting is a research metric; this is the runtime primitive without which no gate survives on a paid plan.
gaps.evidence: openai/codex#19105 ('Memories consuming rate limit disproportionately' — ate the remaining 40% of a weekly limit while idle), #18699, #19732 (idle drain stopped only after generate_memories=false), #24336. NousResearch/hermes-agent#87250 review-fork token usage invisible to telemetry (~30K tokens per review event); #93057 same-model review replays 350k–384k context repeatedly (compaction disabled for cache parity); #90446 refusal loops re-send the full context up to 16 iterations with no token budget; #99661 13+ nudge firings in one ~200-tool-call session; #13534 146 skills cost ~4,400 tokens/turn (~80M tokens/year at 50 turns/day). anthropics/claude-code#71633 skill-creator eval loop 'burns ~50% of a usage window in minutes: full claude -p agent per query x run x iteration, no cost preview or cap'; #91188 (52 comments) compaction reminder nag. alchaincyf/darwin-skill#25: 'evaluating a single skill has high token consumption — any solution?'. volcengine/OpenViking#505 O(n²) semantic reprocessing per stored memory; #4578 bulk ingestion starves interactive session_commit 'for days'; #729 5,405 VLM calls in 5 seconds after a billing failure. affaan-m/ECC#2482 12.8k tokens/turn of always-loaded skill descriptions. deepseek-harness discussion #6574: one request fanned out to 146 subagent sessions and 343,067,904 cache-read tokens (62% of the user's whole history) because only depth, not breadth or total budget, is capped; #6219 token counts omit teammates (2.3x underestimate).
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Loop cost is borne by the user's plan, not the framework author, so no maintainer instruments it; background work is deliberately hidden ('invisible to the user') which also hides its bill; harnesses expose usage per session but not per subsystem; the acceptance-gate literature (SEA: ~90 min/round, 13x the loop) demonstrates that honest gating is the dominant cost and then turns the gate off rather than budgeting it.
gaps.who_cares: Every Codex/Claude Max/Hermes user on a metered plan; enterprise operators of OpenViking/OpenClaw gateways (event-loop stalls, cgroup OOMs); the gate's own credibility (a gate that cannot state its cost will be assumed to be expensive).

gaps.title: Deterministic write-time and update-time lint for learned artifacts (referenced files exist, no placeholder-as-verified, no session-specific facts in global rules, dedup against skills and docs, freshness on host update)
gaps.description: Below any fitness question there is a lint layer that would catch most of the cheap failures users file, is fully deterministic, costs nothing on the pass path, and is invisible until it blocks: (1) structural — frontmatter parses, referenced scripts/references exist, executable skill has code that compiles; (2) evidence — a claim labelled verified/tested must cite a tool-output span, and raw-quote blocks containing placeholder tokens (NNN, HH:MM, <your-path>) can never be codified as fact; (3) scope — ports, hostnames, absolute paths, dates and project codenames observed in one session may not enter global rules without an explicit scope tag; (4) dedup — `skills_list`-before-create against existing skills and against the project knowledge base, with 'patch existing' preferred; (5) classification — memory vs skill vs user-profile routing checked against a rule, not the reviewer's mood; (6) freshness — on `hermes update`/harness upgrade, mark agent-created artifacts needs_review and diff them against a capability baseline; expose 'last verified' age on load. Existing scanners (Hermes skills_guard, OpenClaw regex scanner, NVIDIA SkillEvaluator tier-1, ECC AgentShield) cover security only.
gaps.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent#416 (open since 2026-03-05, filed by the maintainer): validate frontmatter, referenced files exist, Python parses; #25833 (needs-decision): author=executor=judge; Majber's post-update audit in that thread: 10 agent-created skills, several prescribing manual flows now covered by native commands, proposal for a needs_review flag with baseline diff; #89963: placeholder text codified as 'Verified 2026-08-04' and a phantom `_gsc_clear_cache.py` that halted a production run; #6051 learned helplessness from a transient failure; #30220 review misclassifies memory/skill/user content; #101402 skills created with bare frontmatter; #13534 name collision (`superdesign` had name: frontend-design) found only by manual audit; gfpyc/#96704: 3 same-topic skills in 8 hours (x3 clusters), skills duplicating hardware docs, a proposal persisted ~10 s after submission for review, stale skill still naming a retired server months after supersession; hanzckernel (#25833): session ports 5173/8648 generalized into global rules. openclaw/openclaw#107707 plan text written as a skill; #94947 create instead of patch; #80613 raw candidate/confidence/status scaffolding leaked into MEMORY.md. volcengine/OpenViking#3006 74KB skill definitions stored verbatim as single memories; #1486/#3007 five entity files for one relationship, 114 duplicate trajectories; #4413 line-number prefixes accumulate on every merge. affaan-m/ECC#2841 JS camelCase conventions prescribed for a PHP/Laravel repo; #3031 skill quality validator requested. anthropics/claude-code#85075 months-old MEMORY.md loads with no freshness indication; #87783 notes carry claims but no observation sources.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Maintainers keep trying to fix these with prompt text ('do not capture transient failures', 'Be ACTIVE' -> 'nothing to save is normal'), which the digests and issues show does not hold; lint is unglamorous and each rule looks small; there is no shared artifact schema across harnesses so each rule would be written five times; dedup against project docs needs an index nobody maintains; the freshness rule needs a capability baseline that only Git installs provide (Majber/konsisumer agreed on `baseline_unavailable` fail-closed semantics but no PR exists).
gaps.who_cares: Hermes deployments with 100+ agent-created skills (the 182-skill audit found 13 description fixes, 4 deletions, 9 duplicates); OpenClaw Workshop users; OpenViking memory operators; the gate (lint rejects for free what the statistical gate would otherwise have to spend replays on).

gaps.title: An approval surface that does not rot: batched, push-notified, diff-and-evidence-carrying review with expiry and an override path — because queues that rot get set to 'auto'
gaps.description: Staged writes are the only mechanism shown to block 40/40 malicious persistences (MLAS), and every shipped implementation loses in production to approval fatigue: queues are pull-only, unbounded, newest-last, diffless for patches, unreachable from the desktop/gateway, deadlocked on scanner false positives, and expire into un-applyable state. The gap is a review contract: daily (or threshold-triggered) batch with one-line summaries, full diff, evidence pointer, activation history and gate verdict; default disposition computed by the gate (auto-apply on pass, hold on uncertain, block on fail) so the human reviews only holds; holds expire into rejection with a reason; scanner findings are overridable with an audit record; symmetric approve/reject/quarantine/restore paths; and a push channel (chat, tray, PR) rather than a slash command.
gaps.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent#105770 (2026-09-08): 77 pending memory + 164 pending skill writes accumulated silently for ~8 weeks, 'several are already un-applyable'; #76795 queue of 40 records in 12 h with no cap, newest last; #98330/#105759/#104777 desktop has no review surface, `/skills` unavailable; #94353 scanner-refused writes cannot be human-approved -> users write files directly; #99704 multi-id approve applies only the first id, patch diffs empty; #63651 gateway buttons for write approval requested; #91202 approval workflow requested; #106919 explicit opt-in for unattended consolidation requested while keeping the default gate; #16461 guard_agent_created still defaults off. openclaw/openclaw: code default flipped to `autonomous.mode: auto`; #109278 70-second approval window visible only to a paired admin UI; #91266 apply times out because approval wait exceeds the tool watchdog; #93278 apply/reject/quarantine lack symmetric owner-approval paths; #101657/#106134 quarantined proposals are dead-ends; #107555 'Allow' button recorded as rejected. anthropics/claude-code#78398 batched promote/keep/discard adjudication requested; #76186 no recall-only mode; #52706 confirm-on-write closed NOT_PLANNED. openai/codex#19195 memories enabled while prompt says 'Never update memories'; #34668 explicit auditable promotion requested. arXiv 2606.23075 (MLAS): human queue blocked 40/40 but utility cost 'unmeasured'.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Product incentive is autonomy ('the agent learned 12 things today'); harness authors build the staging mechanism and stop before the review UX; the review surface must live where the user already is (chat gateway, desktop, PR) which is per-platform work; and computing a default disposition requires a gate verdict that Camp A does not have, so every item is a hold and the queue rots. The literature treats 'human consent' as a binary control and never measures approval fatigue.
gaps.who_cares: Hermes/OpenClaw operators who turned write_approval on and then off; enterprise deployments that need an audit trail; the whole thesis (the gate only earns the right to auto-apply if the hold path is humane).

gaps.title: One learned-state contract for the several harnesses on one machine (rooted write surface + session-log location + load receipt), so a single gate/ledger/undo serves Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex and DSH without a proxy
gaps.description: Practitioners run several harnesses side by side and want skills and memory to be shared and governed once. The two existing integration styles both fail: LLM proxies (SkillClaw, Reef, Agent Lightning) break harness features and mutate configs; per-harness hooks (ECC, autoharness, OpenViking plugins) fork per target and drift. What is missing is a minimal adapter contract — where the harness roots its learned-state tree, where its session log is and its schema, how to emit/inspect a load receipt, and a hook point on the generic write path (Claude Code PreToolUse permissionDecision, Hermes pre_tool_call, DSH tools/pre-execute + hook-protocol, Codex PostToolUse, OpenClaw before_tool_call, pi tool_call) — plus adapters, so gate, ledger, lint, undo and spend meter are written once. DSH's hook-protocol already runs unmodified Claude Code and Codex hooks.json, which makes a hooks-based adapter run on three harnesses today.
gaps.evidence: AMAP-ML/SkillClaw#20 'I have both openclaw and hermes installed on one machine, can both use skillclaw?'; #35 (Codex) 'deprecated — intrusively interferes with normal execution'; #61 'Broke the Harness'; #71 unauthorized mutation of an unrelated Hermes profile; #18 Claude Code skill call interrupted after first step; #26 Claude Code Skill tool calls not recorded by the session recorder. affaan-m/ECC#2599 skills hardcode ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ but the claude target installs to skills/ecc/<name>/ (breaks hook registrations); #2544 partial installs; #2419 Cursor scaffold wires only sessionStart; #3065 Antigravity target; #1454 hooks.json schema mismatch with Claude Code 2.1.x. volcengine/OpenViking#1283 incompatible with OpenClaw 2026.4.5; #4036 dsh-memory-plugin never published; #591 OpenClaw plugin hangs; #4137 pi extension recall injection destroys prefix caching. NousResearch/hermes-agent#109732 AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md discovery documented wrong; #34782 global self-improving skills have no first-class home across profiles. anthropics/claude-code#31005 (r=483) AGENTS.md / .agents/skills support requested since Aug 2025. deepseek-harness digest: five-phase tool pipeline + hook-protocol run CC/Codex hooks unmodified; SkillMisevo-Gym's GovernableStore already proved one 5-hook contract across Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Each harness moves fast (Hermes 947 commits in four days; OpenClaw breaks plugins per release per #81923) and treats its store layout as internal; proxies are attractive to researchers because they are harness-agnostic by construction but users reject them for breaking features; nobody owns the 'home directory' layer between harnesses; the agentskills.io SKILL.md format standardizes the artifact but not the store, log, receipt or write path.
gaps.who_cares: Multi-harness power users (the Hermes+OpenClaw+Claude Code+Codex population visible in SkillClaw/ECC/OpenViking issues); skill-marketplace curators; every research group that wants real-session data from more than one harness; the builder (adapters are the adoption surface).

gaps.title: A self-serve 'does my store help me?' command that runs on the user's own session logs, cheapest arm first (activation from transcripts), paired replay only where replayable
gaps.description: The scientist lens frames the null-effect audit as a paper; users want it as a one-command tool on their own machine: read ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl (or Hermes/Codex session logs), list every learned artifact with created-by, age, loads, adherence, and — for the subset of sessions whose terminal verification is re-executable in a git-snapshot sandbox — a paired with/without outcome with a null floor from A-vs-A' replays, reported as pass rate ± stddev over 3–5 replays, tri-state, with the cost printed. Output is a per-artifact recommendation (keep / never loaded / loaded-but-ignored / regresses / unknown-needs-N-more-sessions). `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269) does with/without deltas for plugins on authored prompts but not for artifacts the agent wrote to itself nor on the user's real sessions.
gaps.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent#96704 (open, 2026-08-27): community RFC for exactly this in-tree, with three arms, a variance floor ('every case now replays 3 to 5 times... never one number'), the eligible->activated->adhered->effective chain, and 'the cheapest arm needs no model runs and could produce numbers within a day'; production numbers in-thread (70 skills / 3 agents / 5 months: several with use_count=0; 182-skill library audit). anthropics/claude-code#75334 users measuring '4 to 6 identical corrections per data type' by hand; #76408 closed unfixed; vshulcz in #75334: across 43 compactions the summary kept 77% of decisions and 0.2% of commands that ran. openai/codex#23658 'Memories potentially a bad idea... using the wrong Rule at the wrong time can silently lead to unexpected outcomes'. microsoft/SkillOpt#155 tri-state agentic replay proposal endorsed by maintainers; #97 harvest from VS Code sessions requested; #132 Superpowers integration help-wanted ('a result where no candidate beats the current skill is still useful'). Synthesis section F: 7 sessions / 2,062 tool calls on the builder's machine, workspace ops re-executable in a sandbox, externals served from the recording. deepseek-harness marketplace: dsh-verify/dsh-verification/self-optimizing-plugin show demand for local verification tooling.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Research groups do not have users' logs; harness teams have no incentive to publish that their loop is placebo; replay was assumed either trivial or hopeless (Replay Gap) rather than tiered; the activation-only arm is dismissed as too simple to be a contribution although it is the arm users can run today; privacy of session logs means the tool must run locally and report aggregates, which no academic artifact does.
gaps.who_cares: Every user with a growing MEMORY.md/skill library who suspects it is not helping (heavy-scale report #83114; #13534; the 182-skill deployment); framework maintainers who need a benchmark for their loop (hermes#96704 asked for direction); reviewers of memory/skill papers; the builder's killer demo is this command's output.

gaps.title: Learned-state DLP: secret/PII scrubbing, provider and user boundaries, and scope fences for what the loop is allowed to persist and where it may send it
gaps.description: Distinct from the safety lens's provenance taint (untrusted content flowing in): this is trusted content flowing out. Background writers persist credentials from tool output into skills, memories, session captures and even .git/config; memory generators ship transcripts to a different model provider than the one that produced them; shared and multi-agent stores pool one user's or agent's data into another's; and harness permission systems cannot fence the memory directory. Needed: a scrub pass on every persisted artifact and session capture (entropy + pattern + allowlist), a provider-boundary rule (a memory job may only use the provider that produced the source session, or must ask), per-user/per-agent partitioning of shared corpora with visible scope tags, and deny rules that actually cover the learned-state tree.
gaps.evidence: openai/codex#41711 (2026-08-30, open): 'PRIVATE CHAT THREAD EXFILTRATION: Memories exfiltrates local-provider chat content to OpenAI without notice' — confirmed by controlled capture on the stock Windows binary; #33641 exclude recurring automations from global Memories; #18343 scoped memory management. NousResearch/hermes-agent#101351: background review left a plaintext GitHub PAT in the working repo's .git/config and API keys in session captures; #72298 (r=11) passwords shown in Telegram chat; #27182 per-user USER.md isolation for multi-user deployments. AMAP-ML/SkillClaw#11: cross-user aggregation may leak preferences/environment. openclaw/openclaw#65374: dreaming pools every agent's sessions into one corpus and synthesizes first-person memories from other agents; #63829 per-agent vault requested. volcengine/OpenViking#2899: scrub high-entropy secrets before persisting extracted memories and indexing; #4060 identity model for one Hermes serving many end users; #3267 per-user workspace kinds. anthropics/claude-code#87014: permissions.deny Read rules cannot fence the project auto-memory directory; #91738 auto-memory scoped per working directory so unrelated projects share one memory; #85591 Read returns project memory when the global path is requested. affaan-m/ECC observe.sh regex scrub exists but #2278 shows it hanging on unbounded tool I/O.
gaps.why_still_unsolved: Scrubbing is treated as a per-harness regex afterthought; provider-boundary leakage is invisible unless a user captures traffic (#41711 needed a controlled capture); multi-user/multi-agent deployments are newer than the loops (Hermes multi-tenant #34352 is still an open design discussion); and no harness models 'who this artifact is about' as metadata, so scope fences have nothing to key on.
gaps.who_cares: Anyone running a local or non-default provider with memories on (privacy expectation violated); enterprises deploying OpenViking/OpenClaw/Hermes gateways for many users; teams sharing skill stores; security reviewers who must answer 'what did the learning loop copy where'.

surprising_observations: The most-reacted learning-loop-adjacent issue in the largest self-improving agent (hermes-agent#12238, r=38) is not about fitness, safety or gating but about backup and version control for ~/.hermes so users can 'track how their agent evolved over time'. Users want git for their agent's brain before they want CI for it; across ten trackers essentially zero issues ask for statistical acceptance while dozens ask for diff, receipt, undo and budget.

The learning loop is the single most bug-reported subsystem of Hermes: 121 open-or-closed issues carry 'background review' in the title and 89 carry 'curator', and almost all are plumbing (ContextVar read-marks lost across worker threads — fixed three separate times: #79004, #88053, #94324; daemon thread killed at process exit #90683; per-tool instead of per-operation whitelist #105921; result=none misclassified #103235; failed LLM call recorded as 'no change' #83260). A third-party acceptance layer must assume its host loop is silently broken a large fraction of the time and treat 'the loop ran' as a claim to verify.

Gates fail in the field by starving, not by being too strict: with write_approval on, one Hermes operator accumulated 241 staged writes over 8 weeks with no signal (#105770); scanner false positives create approval deadlocks with 'only one way forward: bypassing both the security scan and the approval gate' (#94353); OpenClaw shipped a hash-bound proposal ledger and flipped its default to ungoverned auto. 'Invisible until it blocks' must be stated as: silent on pass, loud on block, and never silent on hold.

The corrupted-working-skill incident (gfpyc in hermes#96704, failure mode 8) is the practitioner twin of Misevolve: a background fork rewrote a user-validated chrome-devtools skill at 02:17 with a wrong rule ('close ALL Chrome windows'), bypassed the ledger by writing the file directly, and the rule 'nearly caused the agent to kill the user's everyday Chrome' — harm arrived through mutation of a previously good artifact, not authorship of a bad one. The same report shows opt-in pinning does not contain it: 'pin gates a name, the loop selects a place' (codification moved to an unpinned sibling within hours). No framework makes user-validated artifacts immutable to unattended writers by default.

Users cite the literature faster than the digests: three papers referenced by Hermes users in Aug–Sep 2026 issues appear in neither landscape_digest.md nor rsi_digest.md — arXiv 2609.11060 (Grounding Agent Memory: environment-probing curation, Microsoft, Sep 10; requested in hermes#107914 as 'verify uncertain memory/skill writes against the live environment before committing'), arXiv 2608.11095 ('Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering': +226% instruction growth over 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repos; requested in #86022 as rationale-attached entries so the curator can delete safely), and arXiv 2607.26637 (filesystem memory lossy-merge; requested in #80791 as a content-preservation rule for consolidation).

The cassette design already has a public design thread to join: microsoft/SkillOpt#155 (July 2026) proposed 'replay mined tasks with a real agentic CLI in a throwaway worktree, gate on the diff'; Microsoft maintainers endorsed it twice with three binding requirements — worktree is not a security boundary, outcomes must be pass/fail/inconclusive, execution off by default — and a contributor volunteered. Building the sandbox-first cassette as a SkillOpt backend plus a Claude Code hook would land in a repo with 17k stars rather than in a new one.

Codex Memories is a user-filed data-exfiltration channel: openai/codex#41711 shows the memory writer selecting a rollout produced by a local/third-party provider and sending its transcript to OpenAI for consolidation, confirmed by controlled capture. Every acceptance-gate paper in the digests models the artifact's safety and none models the loop's egress; the learning loop is itself a network boundary crossing.

Claude Code auto-memory has 139 titled issues and the top user-felt failures are all receipt problems, none fitness problems: whether the index loaded whole/truncated/not at all (#82056, 48 comments; a fourth failure mode — unstable store slug — was discovered in-thread), overflow silently discarding the newest entries so corrections are lost while the corrected text stays loaded (#92998, re-filed after five prior reports were closed by the stale bot), notes carrying claims but not the observations they were bound to (#87783), and months-old memory loading with no freshness signal (#85075). An acceptance layer that shipped only receipts (load, write, cost) and no gate at all would already address the majority of what Claude Code users file.

The production self-evolution layer is churning faster than it is maintained: Prime Intellect closed its entire issue queue on 2026-08-15 (closing '/refine is invisible' unfixed); SkillClaw's last push was 2026-08-17 and its newest issue asks whether it is abandoned; NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution (5.3k stars) is stalled with GEPA skill evolution being a literal no-op (#141) and a validator that rejects every evolved skill; OpenClaw closed a skill-lifecycle request as 'already implemented' via a bot and then shipped a narrower 30/90-day retirement for agent-created skills only. A harness-agnostic layer that lives outside these repos and survives their release cadence has a structural advantage over any in-tree gate.

DeepSeek Harness (223k stars, issues disabled, 6,459 discussions) has no learning loop, and its plugin marketplace has already grown a verification ecosystem in the exact slot the synthesis targets — dsh-verify ('agents self-test and pass, real browsers tell the truth'), dsh-verification ('a completion gate: claimed-done becomes actually-done'), dsh-llm-verifier, dsh-subagent-contract canary, self-optimizing-plugin, and a proposed 'regression gate for the session layer' — while discussion #6574 documents one request fanning out to 146 subagent sessions and 343M cache-read tokens because breadth has no cap. The biggest substrate proves both that third-party verification plugins get built and that budget governance is the first thing users notice missing.

Practitioners independently re-derived the synthesis's measurement discipline before reading any of the papers: in hermes#96704 one operator reports 'single-run comparisons kept lying to us... every case now replays 3 to 5 times and reports a pass rate with stddev, never one number', another proposes the eligible->activated->adhered->effective attribution chain with `adhered` computed without LLM judging, and a third supplies eight write-side failure modes from a 182-skill deployment with reproducible cleanup statistics. The design review for the loop-health funnel has effectively been written by users; the builder's job is to ship it.

Cost is the silent killer of every self-improvement feature in the corpus: Codex users disabled Memories because it drained a weekly quota while idle (#19105/#19732), a Hermes same-model review replays 350k–384k of context repeatedly (#93057), skill-creator's eval loop burns half a usage window in minutes (claude-code#71633), OpenViking reprocesses O(n²) on every stored memory (#505), and darwin-skill's open question is how to afford evaluating one skill (#25). No acceptance-gate paper reports the gate's cost as a fraction of the user's plan; SEA, the one that measured it (13x the loop), responded by disabling the gate. Any shipped gate must print its own bill in the same report it prints its verdicts.
